Title: We must generate habits so that families use financial services without vulnerability and risks
text: Breakfast on saving and microsaving President of the BCU: "We must generate habits for families to use financial services without vulnerability and risks" The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara, stressed the importance of generating tools that encourage the culture of saving of people and companies and that they access services without becoming a source of vulnerability and risks. Bergara participated in the opening of the breakfast called "Savings and microsavings, uses and habits of financial inclusion in lower income segments" organized by the financial savings and credit cooperative FUCEREP together with the Multilateral Fund of Investments (MIF) and the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB). The event was attended by the IDB representative in Uruguay, Juan Jose Taccone; the advisor of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, Martin Vallcorba; the member of the Executive Secretariat of the Pit-Cnt, Fernando Gambera; and the president of FUCEREP, Juan Gervasio. During his message, Bergara reflected that financial deepening contributes to the country's economic development. "From the cultural point of view, it is important to promote healthy savings tools for people and companies," recalled the president of the BCU. In that regard, he stressed the importance of contributing to a culture that fosters these habits. "Just as we take care to make the State's accounts sustainable, the same happens in the administration of families, who must take advantage of financing and financial services avoiding transforming them into a source of vulnerability. and risks," he said. Likewise, the other side of the coin is the economic and financial education that the Central Bank promotes through its BCUEduca economic and financial education program, Bergara concluded.

Bergara particip de la apertura del desayuno denominado Ahorro y microahorro, usos y hbitos de la inclusin financiera en los segmentos de menores ingresos que organiz la cooperativa financiera de ahorro y crdito FUCEREP junto con el Fondo Multilateral de Inversiones (FOMIN) y el Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID). De la instancia participaron el representante del BID en Uruguay, Juan Jos Taccone; el asesor del Ministerio de Economa y Finanzas, Martn Vallcorba; el integrante del Secretariado Ejecutivo del Pit-Cnt, Fernando Gambera; y el presidente de FUCEREP, Juan Gervasio. Durante su mensaje, Bergara reflexion que la profundizacin financiera contribuye al desarrollo econmico del pas. Desde el punto de vista cultural es importante el impulso de herramientas saludables de ahorro de las personas y las empresas, record el presidente del BCU. En ese sentido, subray la importancia de contribuir a una cultura que propicie estos hbitos. As como tenemos el cuidado de hacer sustentable las cuentas del Estado, lo mismo sucede en la administracin de las familias, que deben aprovechar el financiamiento y los servicios financieros evitando transformarlos en una fuente de vulnerabilidad y riesgos, sostuvo. Asimismo, la otra cara de la moneda es la educacin econmica y financiera que el Banco Central impulsa a travs de su programa de educacin econmica y financiera BCUEduca, concluy Bergara. Title: Speech before car dealers about the importance of de-dollarization
text: The president of the BCU spoke to car dealers about the importance of de-dollarization ? The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, spoke to members and directors of the Association of Automotive Brand Dealers (ASCOMA) about the agenda that the institution is carrying out to achieve a quality currency. In his presentation, entitled "The stabilization of inflation in the situation and the de-dollarization strategy," the economist Labat explained the steps taken to have inflation at rates that allow generating better conditions for the de-dollarization process and, as a consequence, achieve greater stability and long-term growth. "We have been using the dollar for 50 years for 50 years and it has become a cultural phenomenon," Labat said. For this objective, he recalled that the first step is to have a convergence of inflation within the target range, which will then allow us to think about the strengthening of the Uruguayan peso as a quality currency. In this sense, Labat summarized the steps taken so far by the BCU to align agents' expectations with the inflation target and reviewed the monetary policy strategy based on the management of the overnight interbank interest rate. "The argument is that the rate allows less volatility for commercial banks, companies and individuals to have a reference in the market and, with a certain stability, make better decisions," he stressed. He then pointed out that having the inflation rate within the target range for a long time is surely the first condition to sustain the de-dollarization process. "One of the issues that we highlight and the difficulties of having a dollarized economy is that it extends economic cycles. In the face of shocks that reach the country, the level of activity deteriorates much more abruptly than in other countries," he said. Subsequently, in reference to how to advance in the de-dollarization of the automotive market in Uruguay, Labat urged that, in the same way that there is a tendency to express credits in indexed units, the first step be taken to express in pesos the prices of the automobile market starting with the used segment. "If someone buys a car from 2002, having the installment in pesos will let them know that they can afford it, because they receive their income in that same currency. I believe that even commercially, and especially thinking about those first segments of the market, (the de-dollarization of prices) would be very useful for sales in the end," concluded the president of the Central Bank. This presentation to the Association of Automotive Brand Dealers is part of the dialogue agenda that the Central Bank has begun in recent weeks with the Association of Private Construction Developers (APPCU), the Chamber of Industries of Uruguay (CIU), the Chamber of Commerce and Services of Uruguay and the Association of Private Banks of Uruguay (ABPU). among other organizations.

En su presentacin, denominada La estabilizacin de la inflacin en la coyuntura y la estrategia de desdolarizacin (/Comunicaciones/Conferencias/Desdolarizacin_ASCOMA_Labat_Presentacion_2021.pdf), el economista Labat explic los pasos dados para contar con la inflacin a tasas que permitan generar mejores condiciones para el proceso de desdolarizacin y, como consecuencia, alcanzar una mayor estabilidad y crecimiento de largo plazo. Llevamos 50 aos donde los uruguayos utilizamos el dlar por razones microeconmicas y se ha convertido en un fenmeno cultural, seal Labat. Para este objetivo record que el primer paso es contar con una convergencia de la inflacin hacia dentro del rango meta lo que luego permitir pensar en el fortalecimiento del peso uruguayo como moneda de calidad. En ese sentido, Labat resumi los pasos dados hasta ahora por el BCU para que las expectativas de los agentes se alineen a objetivo de inflacin y repas la estrategia de la poltica monetaria basada en la gestin de la tasa de inters interbancaria a un da. El argumento es que la tasa permite menor volatilidad para que bancos comerciales, empresas e individuos tengan una referencia en el mercado y, con cierta estabilidad, tomen mejores decisiones, subray. A continuacin seal que contar con la tasa de inflacin dentro del rango meta por un buen tiempo, seguramente sea la primera condicin para sustentar el proceso de desdolarizacin. Una de las cuestiones que nosotros resaltamos y de las dificultades de tener una economa dolarizada es que ampla los ciclos econmicos. Ante shocks que les llegan al pas, el nivel de actividad se deteriora de forma mucho ms abrupta que en otros pases, fundament. Posteriormente, en referencia a cmo avanzar en la desdolarizacin del mercado automotor en Uruguay, Labat inst a que, de la misma manera que existe una tendencia a expresar los crditos en unidades indexadas, se d el primer paso para expresar en pesos los precios del mercado de automviles comenzando por el segmento de usados. Si alguien compra un auto del ao 2002, tener la cuota en pesos le permitir saber que la puede pagar, porque percibe sus ingresos en esa misma moneda. Yo creo que hasta comercialmente, y sobre todo pensando en esos primeros segmentos del mercado, (la desdolarizacin de los precios) sera muy til para la venta al final, concluy el presidente del Banco Central. La presente exposicin ante la Asociacin de Concesionarios de Marcas de Automotores es parte de la agenda de dilogo que ha comenzado el Banco Central durante las ltimas semanas con la Asociacin de Promotores Privados de la Construccin (APPCU), la Cmara de Industrias del Uruguay (CIU), la Cmara de Comercio y Servicios del Uruguay y Asociacin de Bancos Privados del Uruguay (ABPU), entre otras organizaciones. Title: Speech with industrialists about the contribution of a quality currency to price stability and long-term growth
text: The president of the BCU spoke with the industrialists about the contribution of a quality currency to price stability and long-term growth ? The webinar called "The role of industry in the de-dollarization of the economy" was organized by the Chamber of Industries of Uruguay (CIU) and the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU) and took place this morning, May 27, through virtual mode. The opening was in charge of the president of the CIU, Alfredo Ant92a, followed by the president of the BCU, Diego Labat, and the manager of the Bank's Economic Advisory, Gerardo Licandro, who made the presentation of "The role of industry in the de-dollarization of the economy". In his welcoming remarks, Alfredo Ant92a said that it is notorious that behind this call for dialogue there is an objective to try to reduce the exposure of companies, particularly industry, to external shocks. He said that generating a quality market as an alternative to foreign currency would contribute to generating conditions for investment within a framework of changes and elements that when making a decision to invest in machinery, to launch a venture, is fundamental. For his part, Diego Labat thanked the participation in this event with the companies and unions of the industry and indicated that the objective of it is to explain where the BCU wants to go and why these instances of dialogue are being generated. In particular, he said that he understands that exchange and feedback nourish the path to follow in this process of promoting de-dollarization in the economy. He also maintained that since the beginning of his term, monetary policy was aimed at accompanying the economic situation caused by the pandemic and seeking solutions within good practices "aiming to keep the engines always turning." That has been the central concern in these 15 months, Labat said, but without ever stopping "looking at what happens the day after." In this sense, he pointed out that it is necessary to continue taking steps forward and work on the great "must" that the country has in relation to inflation, where he highlights that high inflation and dollarization affect long-term growth, harm monetary policy and financial stability. Therefore, having the north in a process "towards a quality currency" is relevant because once it is imposed it will give many advantages to Uruguayans. Next, Gerardo Licandro made the presentation where he referred to the non-linear effects of inflation on growth linked to the indexation of the financial system, to the fact that dollarization competes with the market in national currency and to the evidence that shows that in Uruguay dollarization affects the financial and real management of Uruguayan companies. Regarding monetary policy, Licandro stressed that in the first place there has been a change in the institutionality of monetary policy where concrete actions have been taken such as the expansion of meetings of the Monetary Policy Committee (COPOM); as well as improvements in transparency, communication and accountability. In relation to progress in terms of transparency and accountability, this involves a deepening of monetary policy communication, such as the publication of meeting minutes that contain comments and projections of the models used in the BCU that allow anticipating the future direction of monetary policy. Finally, Licandro highlighted the dialogue process initiated to achieve in the medium term the de-dollarization of the Uruguayan economy and the consolidation of a quality currency. He also added the importance of talking with the industry and continuing to develop the agenda to exchange and build with the sector since "it is not a matter of prohibiting behaviors but of deepening the dialogue to find a joint path of de-dollarization of the economy that is mutually beneficial."

La apertura estuvo a cargo del presidente de la CIU, Alfredo Anta, luego siguieron el presidente del BCU, Diego Labat, y gerente de la Asesora Econmica del Banco, Gerardo Licandro, quien realiz la presentacin de El rol de la industria en la desdolarizacin de la economa (/Comunicaciones/Conferencias/Labat_Licandro_Desdolarizacion_Presentacion_2021.pdf). En sus palabras de bienvenida, Alfredo Anta dijo que es notorio que detrs de esta convocatoria a dialogar hay un objetivo a tratar de reducir la exposicin de las empresas, en particular de la industria, a los shocks externos. Expres que generar un mercado de calidad como alternativa a la moneda extranjera contribuira a generar condiciones para la inversin dentro de un marco de cambios y elementos que a la hora de tomar una decisin de invertir en maquinaria, de lanzar un emprendimiento, es fundamental. Por su parte, Diego Labat agradeci la participacin a este evento con las empresas y gremiales de la industria e indic que el objetivo del mismo es explicar hacia dnde quiere ir el BCU y por qu se estn generando estas instancias de dilogo. E particular, manifest que entiende que el intercambio y la retroalimentacin nutren el camino a seguir en este proceso de impulsar a la desdolarizacin en la economa. Asimismo, sostuvo que desde el comienzo de su mandato, la poltica monetaria estuvo abocada a acompaar la situacin econmica provocada por la pandemia y a buscar soluciones dentro de las buenas prcticas apuntando a que los motores siguieran siempre girando. Esa ha sido la preocupacin central en estos 15 meses, dijo Labat, pero sin dejar nunca de mirar qu sucede el da despus En este sentido, seal que hay que seguir dando pasos hacia adelante y trabajar en el gran debe que tiene el pas en relacin con la inflacin, donde destaca que una inflacin alta y la dolarizacin afectan el crecimiento de largo plazo, perjudican la poltica monetaria y la estabilidad financiera. Por eso, tener el norte en un proceso hacia una moneda de calidad es relevante porque una vez que est impuesta dar muchas ventajas a los uruguayos. A continuacin, Gerardo Licandro realiz la presentacin donde se refiri a los efectos no lineales de la inflacin sobre e crecimiento vinculados a la indexacin del sistema financiero, a que la dolarizacin compite con el mercado en moneda nacional y a la evidencia que muestra que en Uruguay la dolarizacin afecta la gestin financiera y real de las empresas uruguayas. En lo que refiere a la poltica monetaria, Licandro destac que en primer lugar ha habido un cambio en la institucionalidad de la poltica monetaria en donde se han tomado acciones concretas como la ampliacin de reuniones del Comit de Poltica Monetaria (COPOM); adems de mejoras en transparencia, comunicacin y rendicin de cuentas. Con relacin a los avance en torno a la transparencia y rendicin de cuentas, sta pasa por una profundizacin de la comunicacin de la poltica monetaria como, por ejemplo, la publicacin de las minutas de las reuniones que contienen comentarios y proyecciones de los modelos utilizados en el BCU que permiten anticipar la direccin futura de la poltica monetaria. Por ltimo, Licandro destac el proceso de dilogo iniciado para lograr en el mediano plazo la desdolarizacin de la economa uruguaya y la consolidacin de una moneda de calidad. Asimismo, aadi la importancia que tiene conversar con la industria y seguir elaborando la agenda para intercambiar y construir con el sector ya que no se trata de prohibir conductas sino profundizar el dilogo para encontrar un camino conjunto de desdolarizacin de la economa que sea mutuamente beneficioso. Title: Leading experts discussed The Future of Money and the Financial System
text: September 20, 2017 Leading experts discussed "The Future of Money and the Financial System" Organized by the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU) and within the framework of the initiative called "Day of the Future", promoted for 7 years by the newspaper La Diaria, the Seminar "The Future of Money and the Financial System " was held today. Representatives of agents of the financial system and the related technology sector participated in an exchange environment promoted by the BCU with the aim of understanding and facing the challenges related to new platforms and current technological dynamics. The Enrique V. Iglesias room was the culmination of an initiative through which it seeks to convene broad sectors of civil society, business, academia and politics, through activities that take place throughout the month of September in order to Reflect on events in the medium and long term. The president of the BCU, Mario Bergara, made an initial presentation and then gave rise to an outstanding group of panelists who addressed the new technological platforms applied to financial activity, financial inclusion and electronic means of payment. In his presentation, Bergara reflected on the challenges related to new technologies and the multiple changes they imply in the world of work and education. In the financial field, he said that the first step is to understand what happens in that field. He stated that regardless of the technology "regulatory principles do not change, because the regulator has to defend the interests of unsophisticated agents and prevent systemic risks." Bergara also reiterated that the BCU is preparing to start a pilot plan for the issuance of digital tickets, for which it is already working on technical and logistical aspects. Finally, he also referred to the growing financial inclusion, highlighting the constant increase that has been occurring in the total of payments through electronic means. Juan Pedro Cantera - Superintendent of Financial Services of the BCU Beyond highlighting the potential of new technologies in the sector, among the challenges to be solved he referred to risks such as "the handling of customer information, the risks of access to information for the financial supervisor and the absence of internationally recognized standards." Jorge Ottavianelli - Executive Director of ABPU "Banks are processing technological changes through essential lines such as the digitalization of processes." He also highlighted that some banks are targeting the generation of their own digital platforms and/or partnering with some of them. Sebastian Olivera  President of the Uruguayan Chamber of Fintech "Fintech is a great accelerator of financial inclusion." "It's about pouring that innovation factor into people's quality of life." Florencia Lopez  MEF Advisor "From the point of view of access, since the financial inclusion law we have made important progress. In terms of usage, the data is also very encouraging. Uruguayans are incorporating the benefits of the instruments proposed by financial inclusion." "We must continue working on publicizing the instruments and that is central to economic and financial education." Elisa Facio - President of ANDA "When the law was passed, we saw that several rules of the game were changing , but we also saw that many opportunities were opening up . We understood that we had to accompany our partners in this process of inclusion, and so we promoted it in several ways, integrating all stakeholders." - Nicholas Jodal - CEO of Genexus "What explains everything that's going on is that software is invading the world. For this reason we must develop the capacity to experiment. Uruguay is well positioned to build its future." Title: The president of the BCU spoke to students at Yale University about the opportunities that Uruguay offers for investors
text: March 16, 2022 The president of the BCU spoke to Yale University students about the opportunities that Uruguay offers for investors Economist Diego Labat was invited to participate in the tour of Zonamerica by a group of graduate students The president of the BCU, Diego Labat, in his presentation to students of the MBA of Yale University. Photo: Zonamerica The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, spoke on Monday, March 14, about the opportunities offered by Uruguay to investors, during the visit made to Zonamerica by a group of graduate students from Yale University, United States. In his presentation, Labat explained the highlights of Uruguay as a destination for international investors. In particular, he referred to specific aspects such as the improvement of the monetary policy framework aimed at reducing inflation and anchoring expectations to the target range. In this regard, Labat commented on the recent behavior of inflation in the country, which is above the defined target, and the action of monetary policy in reaction to it through the use of the interest rate as an instrument. Likewise, the president of the BCU recalled that the banking sector in the country exhibits indicators that make it profitable, well capitalized, with high levels of liquidity and low exposure to the region. The international students, who listened to the president of the Central Bank, visited Zonamerica as part of the training agenda offered by the Master of Business Administration (MBA) at Yale University. The objective of the visit was to learn about the business models of seven companies as well as to carry out exchanges with students from the business schools of the University of the Republic, the Catholic University, the University of Montevideo and the ORT University.

Title: Diego Labat at ADM: "Having higher growth rates requires serious reforms that include lowering inflation"
text: May 18, 2022 Diego Labat in ADM: "Having higher growth rates requires serious reforms that include lowering inflation" The president of the BCU spoke this Wednesday, May 18, at the lunch of the Association of Marketing Leaders The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, said that achieving a gradual reduction in inflation is one of the key reforms that Uruguay must carry out to achieve higher growth rates of the economy. The presentation entitled "Challenges and agenda for the Central Bank of Uruguay" was held on Wednesday, May 18, at the luncheon organized by the Association of Marketing Leaders (ADM). In the presentation of the president of the BCU, he reviewed the inflation reduction objective on which the Central Bank's monetary policy is focused. "High inflation affects the long-term growth of companies, because they do not make decisions due to uncertainty, take on less debt than they could, or have inventories above what they need to cover themselves from rising prices," he explained. In this sense, President Diego Labat emphasized that the Central Bank has the challenge of contributing to low inflation: "We care about inflation, because we care about growth. And to grow, we have to have low inflation," he stressed. To this end, he pointed out that lowering inflation is part of the relevant and serious reforms that Uruguay must have on the agenda to achieve higher growth rates. "We understand that the interest rate is the instrument that best transmits the signals we want to give to the market," said the president of the Central Bank. And then he pointed out: "Monetary policy in Uruguay works, we do not always reach results quickly, but it works." In Labat's opinion, perseverance is an attribute that appears repeatedly in countries that have managed to consolidate lower levels of price growth. Referring to the current situation, Labat said that it is true that most of these countries are facing the highest levels of inflation in the last 40 years. However, he urged not to be "conformist", and that situation will sooner or later be overcome. "What is going to happen when the wave passes? Will Uruguay stay at the top or will it accompany the fight against inflation with serious policies? This is the central question that we must ask ourselves," he said. In this regard, he said that the BCU remains focused on monetary policy working on its essential task of lowering inflation: "This is a Central Bank absolutely committed to the long-term objective of gradually lowering inflation (...) Convergence will surely be slower, but we will continue to advance towards the objective," he said. The presentation of the president of the Central Bank also reviewed the BCU's agenda for the financial system to be characterized as solid, innovative and accessible. When analyzing this point, he recalled that Uruguay has comparative advantages to offer financial services to the region and the world based on liberal rules consolidated for decades. Among them, he mentioned the absence of restrictions on the entry or exit of capital, the free exchange market, the free setting of the interest rate and equitable treatment for nationals and foreigners. In addition, he maintained that another of the country's strengths is a solid banking system. In his view, Labat argued that there is a huge opportunity for Uruguay to develop from its financial system. "We have to set clear rules of the game and encourage the private sector to act," he added. Regarding the BCU's agenda for the development of the financial system, he pointed out that improvements were made in specifying immediate money transfers, although he acknowledged that utilization is still low due to the fact that there are still some improvements in compensation. On another note, he highlighted as an achievement the recent approval in Parliament of the law that enables the digitization of checks and electronic checks as instruments of the payment system. He also highlighted as a relevant aspect the process of multi-acquisition, which will allow the improvement of credit and debit card services that are currently offered from the financial sector to the commercial sector. Regarding the first steps taken for the development of the securities market, Labat highlighted the strengthening of the Securities Market Promotion Commission. In the same sense, he highlighted the new possibilities that opened up for the emergence of investment funds, the regulatory review of simplified issuances and the development of instruments in national currency. "We are working because we believe that there are several aspects where it is possible to do things, but it is necessary for the private sector to dialogue and find the best solutions for these things to work," Labat remarked. Finally, President Diego Labat commented on the changes aimed at strengthening innovation with the presentation from the Central Bank of the Financial Innovation Program, Nova BCU. Among the examples of the work, he commented on the work in open banking where it seeks to put the consumer at the center of the discussion. In closing, Labat cited as a recent milestone the submission to the Executive Branch of the bill on Virtual Assets.
text_original: 18 de mayo de 2022 Diego Labat en ADM: Tener tasas de crecimiento ms altas requiere reformas serias que incluyen bajar la inflacin El presidente del BCU expuso este mircoles 18 de mayo en el almuerzo de la Asociacin de Dirigentes de Marketing El presidente del Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, dijo que lograr una reduccin gradual de la inflacin es una de las reformas clave que Uruguay debe concretar para alcanzar mayores tasas de crecimiento de la economa. La presentacin titulada Desafos y agenda para el Banco Central del Uruguay se realiz este mircoles 18 de mayo en el almuerzo organizado por la Asociacin de Dirigentes de Marketing (ADM). En la exposicin del presidente del BCU repas el objetivo de reduccin de inflacin en que se enfoca la poltica monetaria del Banco Central. La inflacin alta afecta el crecimiento de largo plazo de las empresas, porque no toman decisiones por incertidumbre, toman menos deuda de la que podran, o tienen inventarios por encima de lo que necesitan para cubrirse del alza de precios, explic. En ese sentido, el presidente Diego Labat enfatiz que el Banco Central tiene como desafo contribuir a tener una inflacin baja: Nos importa la inflacin, porque nos importa el crecimiento. Y para crecer, tenemos que tener inflacin baja, subray. Para ello, seal que bajar la inflacin es parte de las reformas relevantes y serias que Uruguay debe tener en agenda para alcanzar tasas de crecimiento mayor. Entendemos que la tasa de inters es el instrumento que mejor transmite las seales que queremos dar al mercado, mencion el presidente del Banco Central. Y acto seguido puntualiz: La poltica monetaria en Uruguay funciona, no siempre llegamos a los resultados rpidamente, pero funciona. Ajuicio de Labat, la perseverancia es un atributo que aparece reiteradamente en los pases que han logrado consolidar menores niveles de crecimiento de los precios. Al referirse a la coyuntura actual, Labat dijo que es cierto que la mayora de esos pases enfrenta los mayores niveles de inflacin de los ltimos 40 aos. Sin embargo, inst a no ser conformista, ya esa coyuntura tarde o temprano se superar. Qu va a pasar cuando pase la ola? Uruguay se quedar arriba o va a acompaar con polticas serias el combate a la inflacin? Esta es la pregunta central que debemos realizarnos, puntualiz. En este aspecto dijo que el BCU se mantiene enfocado en que la poltica monetaria trabaje en su cometido esencial de bajar la inflacin: Este es un Banco Central absolutamente comprometido con el objetivo de largo plazo de bajar gradualmente la inflacin (...) Seguramente la convergencia sea ms lenta, pero vamos a seguir avanzando hacia el objetivo, sostuvo. La presentacin del presidente del Banco Central repas tambin la agenda del BCU para que el sistema financiero se caracterice como slido, innovador y accesible. Al analizar ese punto, record que Uruguay tiene ventajas comparativas para ofrecer servicios financieros a la regin y al mundo a partir de reglas liberales consolidadas desde hace dcadas. Entre ellas, mencion la ausencia de restricciones para la entrada o salida de capitales, el mercado de cambios libre, la libre fijacin de la tasa de inters y el tratamiento equitativo para nacionales y extranjeros. Adems, sostuvo que otro de los aspectos fuertes con que cuenta el pas es un sistema bancario slido. En su visin, Labat argument que existe una enorme oportunidad para que Uruguay se desarrolle a partir de su sistema financiero. Tenemos que poner reglas de juego claras e incentivar al sector privado a que acte, aadi. En cuanto a la agenda del BCU para el desarrollo del sistema financiero, seal que se alcanzaron mejoras en concretar las transferencias inmediatas de dinero, aunque reconoci que la utilizacin an es baja debido a que restan algunas mejoras en la compensacin. En otro orden, destac como un logro la reciente aprobacin en el Parlamento de la ley que habilita la digitalizacin de los cheques y los cheques electrnicos como instrumentos del sistema de pagos. Tambin destac como un aspecto relevante el proceso de la multiadquirencia, que permitir la mejora de los servicios de tarjetas de crdito y dbito que se ofrecen actualmente desde el sector financiero al sector comercial. Respecto a los primeros pasos dados para el desarrollo del mercado de valores, Labat destac el fortalecimiento de la Comisin de Promocin del Mercado de Valores. En el mismo sentido destac las nuevas posibilidades que se abrieron para el surgimiento de fondos de inversin, la revisin normativa de emisiones simplificadas y el desarrollo de instrumentos en moneda nacional. Estamos trabajando porque creemos que hay varios aspectos donde es posible hacer cosas, pero es necesario que el sector privado dialogue y encuentre las mejores soluciones para que estas cosas funcionen, remarc Labat. Finalmente, el presidente Diego Labat coment los cambios orientados al fortalecimiento de la innovacin con la presentacin desde el Banco Central del Programa de Innovacin Financiera, Nova BCU. Entre los ejemplos del trabajo, coment el trabajo en banca abierta donde se busca poner al consumidor en el centro de la discusin. Al cierre, Labat cit como un hito reciente el envo al Poder Ejecutivo del proyecto de ley sobre Activos Virtuales.

Title: Diego Labat at Expo Prado 2022: "Low inflation is the best contribution the Central Bank can make to long-term growth"
text: September 12, 2022 Diego Labat at Expo Prado 2022: "Low inflation is the best contribution that the Central Bank can make to long-term growth" The president of the Central Bank spoke at a conference organized by the Confederation of Business Chambers The president of the Central Bank, Diego Labat; and the ministers of Environment, Adrian Pena; and Labor, Pablo Mieres; at Expo Prado 2022 (photo: Presidency of the Republic) The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, spoke at the conference "Opening Time and Reforms" held on Friday, September 9 at Expo Prado 2022, together with authorities from the Executive Branch. During his participation, Labat explained the common denominators of the government's economic policy. As a general framework, he recalled the diagnosis at the beginning of the current government aimed at correcting macroeconomic imbalances. With the outbreak of the pandemic on March 13, 2020, the strategy was twofold: solve short-term problems without forgetting long-term ones. "There was no shortage of vaccines or respirators, but fiscal matters were taken care of, because the government was thinking about the long term," said the president of the BCU. In this sense, he mentioned the relevance of the approval of a Fiscal Rule that leaves Uruguayans better off moving forward. Subsequently, the president of the BCU mentioned that another common denominator is the government's vision regarding the role of the private sector: "Uruguay has a democratic tradition, stability and very good institutions, which it is important that we continue to build (...), so that the private sector can make decisions by investing, developing and growing its companies." Along these lines, Labat stressed that the Government's approach made it possible for the country to grow by more than 4% at the end of the pandemic, recover 58,000 jobs, register 4% more SMEs and that the country has a projection of growing 4.8% in 2022 while the world economy has a growth projection of only 3%. Regarding inflation, Labat said that the average of the last 20 years is at 8%, which represents a structural problem. "One of the issues that the country needs is much lower inflation. The best contribution that the Central Bank can make to Uruguay's long-term growth is to have low inflation, because the inflation we have today distorts and has effects on the everyday decisions of companies, which decide not to go into debt, to have more inventory than necessary, which they would not need with lower inflation," said the president of the BCU. With this objective, he described that the new monetary policy framework was implemented, with a modern methodology, use of the interest rate and signs of greater transparency. "In mid-2021, inflation began to rise. Today we are better than Chile, Brazil and similar to the United States or Europe. In any case, that does not satisfy us and we have to make the effort because those countries are going to begin to see the results and we also want to start seeing them," said economist Labat. Regarding exchange rate policy, he recalled that Uruguay has a floating exchange rate regime, which is the best for a small country with an open economy, because it allows absorbing any shock from abroad. The president explained that the Central Bank can intervene, when appropriate, but said that the greatest effort in the foreign exchange market is to work on its transparency. As examples, he cited the publication of the price of the exchange rate every 15 minutes or that public companies operate directly in the market and not with the Central Bank. Finally, regarding the strategy for the stock market and the Payment System, he mentioned that it seeks to give clear rules and signals for the market to act. The example of these rules is the reactivation of the Securities Market Promotion Commission (CPMV) and the Payment System Roadmap published in 2020. The aforementioned Roadmap made it possible to reach one of the milestones on September 1st: completing the process called "multi-acquiring", which enables businesses to have a single contract with all debit, credit and electronic money cards of MasterCard and VISA. The conference in which Labat participated was organized by the Confederation of Business Chambers and also had the presentations of the Minister of Labor and Social Security, Pablo Mieres; and the Minister of Environment, Adrian Pena.
text_original: 12 de septiembre de 2022 Diego Labat en la Expo Prado 2022: Una inflacin baja es el mejor aporte que el Banco Central puede hacer al crecimiento de largo plazo El presidente del Banco Central expuso en una conferencia organizada por la Confederacin de Cmaras Empresariales El presidente del Banco Central, Diego Labat; y los ministros de Ambiente, Adrin Pea; y Trabajo, Pablo Mieres; en la Expo Prado 2022 (foto: Presidencia de la Repblica) El presidente del Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, expuso en la conferencia Tiempo de Apertura y Reformas realizada el viernes 9 de setiembre en la Expo Prado 2022, junto con autoridades del Poder Ejecutivo. Durante su participacin, Labat explic los denominadores comunes de la poltica econmica del gobierno. Como marco general, record el diagnstico al inicio de la actual gestin de gobierno orientado a realizar correcciones de los desequilibrios macroeconmicos. Con la irrupcin de la pandemia el 13 de marzo de 2020, la estrategia fue doble: resolver los problemas de corto plazo sin olvidar los de largo plazo. No faltaron vacunas ni respiradores, pero se cuid lo fiscal, porque el gobierno estaba pensando en el largo plazo, subray el presidente del BCU. En ese sentido, mencion la relevancia que tuvo la aprobacin de una Regla Fiscal que deja a los uruguayos mejor parados hacia adelante. Posteriormente, el presidente del BCU mencion que otro denominador comn es la visin del Gobierno respecto del rol que tiene el sector privado: Uruguay tiene tradicin democrtica, estabilidad e instituciones muy buenas, que es importante que sigamos construyendo (...), para que el sector privado tome decisiones invirtiendo, desarrollando y haciendo crecer sus empresas. En esa lnea, Labat destac que el enfoque del Gobierno posibilit que a la salida de la pandemia el pas creciera ms de 4%, recuperara 58.000 puestos de trabajo, se registrara un 4% ms de Pymes y que el pas tenga una proyeccin de crecer 4,8% en 2022 mientras que la economa mundial tiene una proyeccin de crecimiento de solo un 3%. En cuanto a la inflacin, Labat dijo que el promedio de los ltimos 20 aos est en 8%, lo que representa un problema estructural. Una de las cuestiones que necesita el pas es una inflacin bastante ms baja. El mejor aporte que el Banco Central puede hacer al crecimiento de largo plazo de Uruguay es tener una inflacin baja, porque la inflacin que tenemos hoy distorsiona y tiene efectos en las decisiones de todos los das de las empresas, que deciden no endeudarse, tener ms inventario del necesario, lo que no necesitaran con una inflacin ms baja, sostuvo el presidente del BCU. Con ese objetivo describi que se implement el nuevo marco de poltica monetaria, con una metodologa moderna, utilizacin de la tasa de inters y seales de mayor transparencia. A mitad de 2021 la inflacin empez a subir. Hoy estamos mejor que Chile, Brasil y parecidos a Estados Unidos o Europa. De todas maneras, eso no nos conforma y tenemos que hacer el esfuerzo porque esos pases van a empezar a ver los resultados y nosotros tambin queremos empezar a verlos, dijo el economista Labat. Sobre la poltica cambiara record que Uruguay tiene un rgimen de tipo de cambio flotante, que es el mejor para un pas pequeo con una economa abierta, porque permite absorber cualquier shock proveniente del exterior. El presidente explic que el Banco Central puede llegar a intervenir, cuando corresponda, pero dijo que el mayor esfuerzo en el mercado cambiario es trabajar en su transparencia. Como ejemplos cit la publicacin del precio del tipo de cambio cada 15 minutos o que las empresas pblicas operen directamente en el mercado y no con el Banco Central. Finalmente, en cuanto a la estrategia para el mercado de valores y el Sistema de Pagos, mencion que se busca dar reglas y seales claras para que el mercado acte. El ejemplo de esas reglas es la reactivacin de la Comisin de Promocin del Mercado de Valores (CPMV) y la Hoja de Ruta del Sistema de Pagos publicada en 2020. La mencionada Hoja de Ruta permiti alcanzar el Io de setiembre uno de los hitos: completar el proceso denominado multiadquirencia, que habilita a que los comercios tengan un nico contrato con todas las tarjetas de dbito, crdito y dinero electrnico de MasterCard y VISA. Title: Diego Labat on good practices in financial consumer protection: "We seek to provide incentives for things to be done better"
text: October 18, 2022 Diego Labat on good practices in financial consumer protection: "We seek to provide incentives to do things better" The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay spoke at an event of LSQA and the Trade Defense League The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, spoke on Tuesday, October 18, about the impact of governance systems on entrepreneurship, the business climate and investments in Uruguay. The conference was held at the launch of the G program, designed by LSQAS. Ay Quality Austria and the Trade Defense League (LIDECO) with the aim of helping organizations improve their governance practices in the dimensions of compliance management and anti-bribery management. Labat raised the need to discern when there should be mandatory compliance rules or an incentive scheme that ultimately allows for better governance, particularly in the financial system. As an example of an incentive scheme, Labat mentioned the project " Guide to good practices in consumer protection of financial services", which the Superintendence of Financial Services (SSF) released in August. Regarding this initiative, Labat recalled that companies will be able to choose and show certification in compliance with these good practices or, otherwise, they will be able to choose not to be certified, although they must always (in both cases) comply with the minimum rules required at the regulatory level. The example of good practices represents an incentive for companies on their own to seek to have a better government in a natural and not forced way. "(With the code of good practices) we seek to give incentives for those who want to be certified to be certified and for those who want to do things better to do so," Labat said. In addition, the conference of the president of the Central Bank reviewed that Uruguay has solid and stable rules and institutions. Regarding the public sector, Labat mentioned the changes introduced in the last National Budget for the governance of public companies. "It is about modernizing and having better accountability; demand that public companies have certain results and that the results are increasingly measurable," he stressed. As for the BCU, he remarked that there is a corporate governance that he described as "an example" and pointed out that the Institution promotes better governance for the entire financial system. "We have to start expanding more and more the substance and not the form. That is, not only worry about having independent directors, but that the decisions really have substance and that corporate governance effectively works," Labat said.

Title: The president of the BCU reiterated the importance of building a payment system that operates quickly
text: October 24, 2022 The president of the BCU reiterated the importance of building a payment system that operates quickly Economist Diego Labat spoke in Washington during the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank The Future of nn leui n Latin America #NewEcon #NewEcon In a meeting organized by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, highlighted the importance for Uruguay of developing a payment system that operates quickly, similar to what happens in the countries of the region. Labat spoke on October 14 at the forum "The Future of Fintech in Latin America," held during the Annual Meetings of the Boards of Governors of the IMF and the World Bank in Washington, United States. In the BCU president's vision, the strategy also includes the use of a digital currency issued by the Central Bank (CBDC), which had its pilot experience in 2017. "Uruguay carried out a very successful pilot project with specific technology. It allowed us to learn a series of things and then share our experience with other countries. We have not yet scaled up the project, but we anticipate that we will have new advances next year," said the president of the BCU. However, Labat said that the goal at present is to have a payment system platform that meets the best existing standards. "Our main goal is to build a fast payment system, similar to the experience we have in the region," he said; and remarked: "For us there are no contradictions between implementing a digital currency developed by the Central Bank and having a fast payment system." Likewise, the president of the Central Bank emphasized the importance of having established an Innovation Observatory in 2020 that allowed establishing an "ambitious agenda" together with the industry. "The goal is to find solutions that allow the industry to take advantage of the advantages of technology and innovation for the benefit of users. Our role as regulators involves being sure that the industry works according to the best standards," he stressed. In this sense, he recalled that the Innovation Office and the industry investigated, worked on different projects and then regulations were issued on matters such as digital onboarding, cloud operations, open banking and virtual assets. "The Central Bank's motto is to give space to innovation without losing financial stability," Labat concluded. The Annual Meetings of the Boards of Governors of the IMF and the World Bank brought together central bank officials, finance and development ministers, parliamentarians, private sector executives, representatives of civil society organizations, and academics from October 10 to 16, 2022, to discuss topics such as the global economic outlook, the end of poverty and economic development.
text_original: 24 de octubre de 2022 El presidente del BCU reiter la relevancia de construir un sistema de pagos que opere con celeridad El economista Diego Labat expuso en Washington durante las Reuniones Anuales del Fondo Monetario Internacional y el Banco Mundial The Future of nn leui n Latn America #NewEcon En un encuentro organizado por el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI), el presidente del Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, destac la importancia que tiene para Uruguay desarrollar un sistema de pagos que opere con celeridad, de forma similar a lo que sucede en los pases de la regin. Title: Invited by the Commercial and Industrial Center of Salto, the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay presented the economic prospects outlined by the current administration
text: November 04, 2022 Invited by the Commercial and Industrial Center of Salto, the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay presented the economic perspectives outlined by the current administration Diego Labat: "The BCU works in a transparent and open way, taking what has been done by previous generations, to build an innovative financial system that is open to the world" The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay, Diego Labat, in Salto. Photo: Commercial and Industrial Center of Salto On October 27, at the event "Thinking about what is coming" of the cycle of talks at the Commercial and Industrial Center of Salto, the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, spoke together with the former president of the Uruguayan Chamber of Information Technologies, Leonardo Loureiro, and the president of the Business Confederation of Uruguay, Juan Martinez. During his conference, Labat highlighted some achievements made by the BCU in this period. The focus of his speech was on the innovation of the policies outlined by the Board of Directors, on the permanent coordination between institutions in the public and private spheres of the country. As a framework for his presentation, Labat spoke of the implementation of a fiscal rule that makes it possible for this government and the next ones to have limited spending, that the debt is sustainable and does not grow, and in this way its payment to future generations is not endangered, a fundamental aspect for the economic stability of the country. During his participation in the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank in Washington in the second week of October, Labat mentioned that he was able to see how from other organizations and regions of the world Uruguay is seen as a serious country, with a solid financial system and that provides confidence. In this sense, he illustrated with graphs the place that the country occupies in the ranking of several prestigious rating agencies, which place it in the best position in the region in terms of indices of political stability and democracy, adherence to the rule of law, absence of civil disorder, level of conflict, and perception of corruption. The president of the BCU, in that presentation, also gave an account of the development of the institutional leadership that had to be adapted to reality when he took office in March 2020. The BCU promoted the lending of money when the pandemic began, that the economy continued to function, beyond the opinions of concern about falling into the credit crunch, which is the cut off of credit and the chain of payments; But that did not happen. "The work of high beams and low beams worked because despite the fact that we had our hand outstretched, from day one we were saying: we are going to implement this modality of policy but when normality returns, we are going to aim to control inflation, and also, reach levels much lower than those we have today," Labat stressed. The hierarch mentioned the improvements implemented to strengthen the communication of monetary policy: quantity and quality of the information included in the Monetary Policy Report (IPOM) in which it has been sought to be increasingly transparent so that it can have a very broad vision of how the economy is doing in Uruguay and the reason for the decisions that are made. He also pointed out that the meetings of the Monetary Policy Committee (COPOM) were doubled from four to eight times a year, a fact that allows maintaining the necessary fine tuning and acting when required without having to wait three months. From the BCU, Labat said, not only does it think about the internal economy, but it also focuses on the region and the world, because Uruguay is a small country, which has to open up and think outwards. At the beginning of the Central Bank's management, the country was behind compared to other countries in the region according to indicators of the use of some products that had not yet been implemented here, but based on this and a lot of our own research, changes are being made to modernize the payment system in Uruguay. As an example of this, Labat listed the improvement in immediate transfers, in the approval of the bill for the digitization of checks and the changes with the implementation of multi-acquisition, among others. The president of the BCU highlighted the creation in 2020 of the financial innovation program - NOVA BCU that seeks, in a permanent dialogue with the industry, to study, research and change what is necessary in the financial system on issues such as digital onboarding, open banking and platforms for loans between people and for collective financing projects. and the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing. In relation to virtual assets, Labat said that at the end of last year a white paper was published with the entire position of the BCU regarding virtual assets: "Our premise and way of acting was always to seek to give signals to the private sector; We announced that we would send a law to Parliament, we made a roadmap and we continue working, because the important thing is predictability." Finally, Labat said that the BCU is working in an open way because he considers that it should be a strategy not only of the Central Bank but that it has transversal aspects that go in the same line with the Ministry of Economy and other State agencies, with the aim of generating bases and adding efforts to what has been done in these two years. always taking into account what previous governments and previous generations have built. "In this way we are building this Uruguay, step by step, without believing that we know everything and that then we will do well abroad naturally. In this way we work to continue building a country that in the future we all want to live in and feel proud of," concluded the president of the BCU.

Title: The BCU announced the first edition of the "Economy and Gender in the Financial System" Award
text: May 12, 2023 The BCU announced the first edition of the "Economy and Gender in the Financial System" Award The president of the Central Bank, Diego Labat, led the launch ceremony of the award that promotes the preparation of academic works on the subject On the morning of Friday, May 12, the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU) launched the first edition of the "Economy and Gender in the Financial System" Award. The call promotes the development of knowledge in the detection of gender gaps in the use of the financial system, in the performance of certain positions, in the conformity or adaptation of the financial system with the needs and characteristics of all people, among others. The objective is to promote the generation of knowledge that interrelates the economy and the gender perspective, to detect and reduce these gender gaps within the financial system. Researchers, professionals and students, born or resident in Uruguay, may participate in this call. Individual studies or co-authorship with a maximum of three members will be admitted. At the opening of the event, the manager of Planning and Strategic Management of the Central Bank, Alfredo Alio, stressed that the Award is the realization of the work that the BCU has been carrying out for years through the Quality Management Model with Gender Equity as well as maturation, with the support of the Economic Advisory of the Institution. of the idea of facing from a transversal perspective the generation of a field of research outside the bank. For his part, the president of the BCU, Diego Labat, said that it is a pleasure for the Central Bank to launch this award that is based on the idea that "we always have to do a little more (...), a concept that is valid for people, but also for organizations." "We have metrics, which are very good, but nevertheless we think that we should always go a little further. (...) With the detection of internal gaps, we think about all the things that the BCU can contribute to the elimination of gender gaps and other gaps, based on the fulfillment of its functions," she said. Labat added that this initiative helps to obtain a more accurate diagnosis of reality, contributing to generate better policies, which then help to cut biases and raise barriers. "This type of research is an opportunity to encourage knowledge about different aspects. We will see what prospects the works have, but clearly it will be a very useful tool for the generation of knowledge and for its practical application," said the president of the BCU. The jury that will evaluate the works, for which the application period of works began until September 30, 2023 inclusive, is made up of Barbara Mainzer (Association of Private Banks of Uruguay), Veronica Amarante (University of the Republic), Magdalena Furtado (UN Women), Soledad Giudice (Association of Bank Employees of Uruguay) and Gerardo Licandro (BCU).

Title: The president of the BCU spoke at Somos Uruguay about the new monetary policy framework
text: The president of the BCU spoke at Somos Uruguay about the new monetary policy framework Economist Diego Labat participated in Somos Uruguay's L92nea de Encuentro space on the night of Wednesday, May 31 The president of the board of directors of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, spoke on Wednesday, May 31, 2023, to representatives of companies that participated in the L92nea de Encuentro space, organized by Somos Uruguay. In the presentation, called "The new monetary policy framework", Labat reviewed the importance for the country of having low inflation, since it generates positive effects on income redistribution and long-term growth, as well as contributes to the de-dollarization of the financial management of companies. "The world finds it strange that Uruguay for 20 years has lived peacefully with inflation of 8% (...) High inflation is not free, because it generates problems in the management of companies and that affects growth," said the president of the BCU. With this focus, the president of the Central Bank ratified the importance of the inflation targeting regime, which is used in most countries of the world. In this sense, Labat recalled the Central Bank's strategy towards a quality currency, which has as pillars the commitment to lower inflation, the use of the interest rate, the strengthening of transparency in communication, de-dollarization and free floating. Regarding the evaluation of the current monetary policy framework, Labat said that there are good results from the current management, but there is still work to be done: "We are not conformists, we have good results, but we have a long way to go," he said. For this reason, Labat recalled the importance of addressing inflation, but also the focus on his expectations. "If inflation is higher than the target range, the Central Bank will react with the interest rate hike. We want to be transparent so that all agents understand how we reason and react as we want (...) We are concerned about making the agents understand and that expectations converge," he stressed. In this regard, President Labat said that the inflation expectations of the agents surveyed by the Central Bank are rigid, but they are evolving in the right direction. "In the last 36 months, expectations have been below the historical average," Labat said. Regarding the projections, the president of the BCU recalled that it is necessary for monetary policy to remain in a contractionary phase: "The reduction in the interest rate will be as slow as necessary for expectations to converge towards what the Central Bank expects," he added. Finally, on the exchange rate, Labat confirmed that the Central Bank reserves the right to intervene when there are real conditions that warrant it. Meanwhile, the focus is on providing transparency so that all actors who need to buy or sell do so through the market. The presentation of the president of the BCU (see attached video) also referred to the lines of work of the Institution in the financial system, innovation, payment system, prevention of money laundering and financing of terrorism, consumer defense and sustainable finance.
text_original: 01 de junio de 2023 El presidente del BOU expuso en Somos Uruguay sobre el nuevo marco de poltica monetaria El economista Diego Labat particip del espacio Lnea de Encuentro de Somos Uruguay en la noche del mircoles 31 de mayo El presidente del directorio del Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, expuso este mircoles 31 de mayo de 2023 ante representantes de empresas que participaron del espacio Lnea de Encuentro, que organiza Somos Uruguay. En la presentacin, denominada El nuevo marco de poltica monetaria, Labat repas la importancia que tiene para el pas contar con una inflacin baja, ya que genera efectos positivos en la redistribucin del ingreso y en el crecimiento de largo plazo, as como contribuye a la desdolarizacin de la gestin financiera de las empresas. La inflacin alta no es gratis, porque genera problemas en la gestin de las empresas y eso afecta el crecimiento, dijo el presidente del BCU. Con ese foco, el presidente del Banco Central ratific la importancia que tiene el rgimen de metas de inflacin, que se utiliza en la mayora de los pases del mundo. En ese sentido, Labat record la estrategia del Banco Central hacia una moneda de calidad, que tiene como pilares el compromiso con una inflacin ms baja, la utilizacin de la tasa de inters, el fortalecimiento de la transparencia en la comunicacin, la desdolarizacin y la libre flotacin. Respecto a la evaluacin del marco actual de poltica monetaria, Labat dijo que hay buenos resultados de la gestin actual, pero an queda trabajo por hacer: No somos conformistas, tenemos buenos resultados, pero nos falta mucho, seal. Title: The presidents of the central banks of Uruguay and Argentina signed a letter of intent to expand operations in local currencies
text: July 04, 2023 The presidents of the central banks of Uruguay and Argentina signed a letter of intent to expand operations in local currencies The objective is to promote the development of low-cost financial instruments for operations involving the Uruguayan peso and the Argentine peso The president of the Central Bank of the Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, and the president of the Central Bank of the Republic Argentina (BCRA), Miguel Pesce, signed a letter of intent aimed at promoting the development of low-cost financial instruments for operations involving the Uruguayan peso and the Argentine peso. The letter was signed on Monday, July 3, within the framework of the LXII Meeting of Ministers of Economy and Presidents of Central Banks of Mercosur, which took place in Puerto Iguazu, province of Misiones (Argentina). The agreement aims to incorporate payments related to trade in services (except payments related to financial services), transfers for family support and allow the transfer of resources to be denominated indistinctly in Argentine pesos or Uruguayan pesos. The technical and operational aspects and the requirements for its use will be stipulated through agreements between both institutions. The commitment states that the central banks of both countries will work to expand the operations supported in the Local Currency Payment System (SML) in force between Uruguay and Argentina. This commitment is based on the idea that the reduction of transaction costs to trade in local currencies, through the SML, represents a stimulus for foreign trade operations. The SML allows economic agents in Uruguay and Argentina to become familiar with the use of each other's currencies, in addition to promoting progress in the process of economic integration and strengthening links between institutions, increasing the liquidity and efficiency of the exchange market between the Argentine peso and the Uruguayan peso. The SML in force between the two countries allows payments to be made for trade operations of documented goods in the currency of the exporting country. Likewise, transfers classified as retirements and pensions are admitted, when there is a bilateral agreement signed between the social security institutes of both countries.
text_original: 04 de julio de 2023 Los presidentes de los bancos centrales de Uruguay y Argentina firmaron una carta de intencin para ampliar las operaciones en monedas locales El objetivo es propiciar el desarrollo de instrumentos financieros de bajo costo para operaciones que involucren al peso uruguayo y al peso argentino El presidente del Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, y el presidente del Banco Central de la Repblica Argentina (BCRA), Miguel Pesce, firmaron una carta de intencin orientada a propiciar el desarrollo de instrumentos financieros de bajo costo para operaciones que involucren al peso uruguayo y al peso argentino. La carta se rubric el lunes 3 de julio en el marco de la LXII Reunin de Ministros de Economa y Presidentes de Bancos Centrales del Mercosur, que se desarroll en Puerto Iguaz, provincia de Misiones (Argentina). El acuerdo tiene el objetivo de incorporar los pagos relacionados con el comercio de servicios (excepto los pagos referentes a servicios financieros), las transferencias en concepto de ayuda familiar y permitir que la transferencia de recursos pueda ser denominada indistintamente en pesos argentinos o pesos uruguayos. Los aspectos tcnicos, operacionales y los requisitos para su utilizacin se estipularn a travs de acuerdos entre ambas instituciones. El compromiso establece que los bancos centrales de ambos pases trabajarn para ampliar las operaciones admitidas en el Sistema de Pagos en Moneda Local (SML) vigente entre Uruguay y Argentina. Este compromiso se apoya en la idea respecto a que la reduccin de los costos de transaccin para comerciar en monedas locales, a travs del SML, representa un estmulo para las operaciones de comercio exterior. El SML permite a los agentes econmicos de Uruguay y Argentina familiarizarse con el uso de la moneda del otro pas, adems de promover avances en el proceso de integracin econmica y fortalecer los vnculos entre las instituciones, aumentando la liquidez y la eficiencia del mercado de cambio entre el peso argentino y el peso uruguayo. El SML vigente entre ambos pases permite cursar pagos de operaciones de comercio de bienes documentadas en la moneda del pas exportador. Asimismo, se admiten las transferencias clasificadas como jubilaciones y pensiones, cuando exista acuerdo bilateral suscripto entre los institutos previsionales de ambos pases.

Title: The BCU presented to industrialists the improvements in the operation with Argentina of the Payment System in Local Currencies
text: July 13, 2023 The BCU presented to industrialists the improvements in the operation with Argentina of the Payment System in Local Currencies The president of the Central Bank, Diego Labat, was received by the Board of Directors of the Chamber of Industries of Uruguay The Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU) presented on Thursday, July 13, to the Board of Directors of the Chamber of Industries of Uruguay (CIU) the improvements of the Local Currency Payment System (SML) with Argentina, which will be implemented through the letter of intent signed between both central banks during the Meeting of Ministers of Economy and Presidents of Central Banks of Mercosur. held in Puerto Iguazu, Argentina. In the presentation to the Uruguayan industrialists, the president of the BCU, Diego Labat, and the head of Infrastructure and Payment System Projects of the BCU, Antonio Zarrillo, were received by the president of the CIU, Fernando Pache; the president of the Foreign Trade Commission, Washington Duran; and the former president of the CIU, Alfredo Antia. The SML between the two countries allows payments to be made for trade operations of goods and services (except financial ones), documented in Uruguayan pesos or in Argentine pesos. Likewise, transfers classified as retirements and pensions are admitted, when there is a bilateral agreement signed between the social security institutes of both countries. "The changes we mentioned are already in the letter we signed with the Central Bank of the Republic Argentina. Now, it needs the approval of the legal areas of both central banks and within a month it will be operational," said the president of the BCU. The signed commitment establishes that the central banks of both countries will work to expand the operations admitted in the Local Currency Payment System in force between Uruguay and Argentina. This commitment is based on the idea that the reduction of transaction costs to trade in local currencies, through the SML, represents a stimulus for foreign trade operations. Finally, Labat said that the BCU will work together with the CIU "case by case" to resolve the difficulties that arise in this operation.

El compromiso firmado establece que los bancos centrales de ambos pases trabajarn para ampliar las operaciones admitidas en el Sistema de Pagos en Moneda Local vigente entre Uruguay y Argentina. Title: Diego Labat in front of technology companies: "Financial services require more and more interoperability and interconnections between all players"
text: July 28, 2023 Diego Labat to technology companies: "Financial services increasingly require interoperability and interconnections between all players" The president of the Central Bank participated in a meeting with members of the Uruguayan Chamber of Information Technologies The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay, Diego Labat, at a meeting of the Uruguayan Chamber of Information Technologies. The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, participated in a meeting organized by the Uruguayan Chamber of Information Technologies (CUTI), called "Cuti connect". The event, held on Thursday, July 27, brought together members of the Chamber and actors in the financial industry to think about an integrating vision towards the year 2030. Based on this proposal, Labat referred to the value that technology companies bring to the financial business. "In mass financial services we are at a time where providers have the need to go all out and, for this, more and more interoperability and interconnections between all players are required. We are in a world where there is less and less space to go for niche markets. I believe that banks play a great role in ensuring that the ecosystem is on solid foundations," said the president of the BCU. Regarding the Central Bank, Labat recalled that its role is to ensure the solid functioning of the financial system that allows it to develop its full potential. To this end, he said that in the last three years the BCU has sought to change the way of thinking about the regulation of the financial industry, looking at the functions rather than the different compartments of the system. In this sense, the president of the BCU stressed the importance of thinking about a regulation based on generic principles and, at the same time, strengthening supervision: "I imagine a regulation with general principles rather than detailed rules; and a much stronger supervision, which has knowledge of the business. That's the way I think it's going to evolve," Labat said. Likewise, the president of the Central Bank said that there is an important space for cooperation between all actors for the system to evolve. "One of the messages we pass on is that the BCU is the guarantee that things will improve (...) I trust that by 2030 the entire industry will have achieved a very strong leap in infrastructure quality and, for this, we are the guarantee that if the industry does not achieve it, we will have to do it ourselves," he said. At the CUTI meeting, together with the president of the Central Bank, the country lead of Mercado Pago, Patricia Blanco; the executive director of the Association of Private Banks of Uruguay, Barbara Mainzer; and the president of Banco Republica, Salvador Ferrer. The secretary general of the CUTI, Amilcar Perea, was in charge of moderating the meeting, an opportunity in which he highlighted the importance of the call made by the BCU to the industry to promote innovation: "We can stand from different sides and have different visions, but the Central Bank is playing the role of encouraging us all and sitting down to dialogue," Perea highlighted.

Title: The president of the BCU spoke to tourism entrepreneurs about monetary policy, economic situation and payment system
text: August 08, 2023 The president of the BCU spoke to tourism entrepreneurs about monetary policy, economic situation and payment system Economist Diego Labat participated in a meeting organized by the Uruguayan Chamber of Tourism The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, was invited to a meeting with businessmen, organized by the Uruguayan Chamber of Tourism. The instance, called CAMTUR Focus, proposed a space for exchange on the challenges of the sector, where Labat and the president of Banco Republica, Salvador Ferrer, spoke. Title: Diego Labat on the decline in inflation: "The task is not finished, but we are where we wanted to be"
text: August 31, 2023 Diego Labat on the decline in inflation: "The task is not finished, but we are where we wanted to be" The president of the Central Bank spoke at the luncheon of the Association of Marketing Leaders The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, told businessmen on Thursday, August 31, that the current level of inflation represents the result of the target set by the BCU in 2020, although he emphasized that "the task is not finished." Labat spoke at the luncheon of the Association of Marketing Leaders (ADM), where he gave a presentation called "Low inflation as a pillar of growth". In that instance, before representatives of the country's main companies, the president of the Central Bank highlighted the virtue of the inflation targeting regime and the use of the interest rate as an instrument to achieve low and stable inflation. "Our commitment is to use the instrument. When the deviation of inflation is upwards, we raise the interest rate and when the deviation of inflation is downwards, we lower the interest rate," Labat summarized. In his presentation, the president of the BCU reviewed the way in which the Central Bank has managed to bring inflation to the current level (4.79% year-on-year as of July 2023) within the target range of 3%-6%. "Inflation is where we expected it to be in 2020, the objective for which we have worked. This is part of what the Central Bank has done, but it is also part of the line that economic policy and the government have worked on. It seemed that in Uruguay this was not viable, but this can be done. That is why inflation is at 4.79%," Labat said. However, the president of the BCU recalled that there is still work to be done: "The process is not finished, the inflation targeting regime in Uruguay is under construction, where many agents have not yet internalized it, where we have to continue working, the benefits have been seen and will continue to be seen going forward." And he added: "The task is not finished, but we are in the place where in 2020 we said we wanted to be." In this sense, Labat said that there is still work pending, for example, to achieve a decrease in the inflation expectations of agents such as companies, which have exhibited improvements in their trend. "The expectations of businessmen and analysts in general have improved and are on the path we want," concluded the president of the Central Bank. Labat's presentation was accompanied by the vice president of the Central Bank, Washington Ribeiro; the Minister of Economy and Finance, Azucena Arbeleche; the Secretary of the Presidency of the Republic, Alvaro Delgado; the deputy secretary of the Presidency of the Republic, Rodrigo Ferres; and the director of the Office of Planning and Budget, Isaac Alfie, among other authorities of state entities and companies.

Title: The president of the BCU confirmed that consolidating low inflation will have a positive impact on the growth of the economy
text: September 07, 2023 The president of the BCU confirmed that consolidating low inflation will have a positive impact on the growth of the economy Diego Labat recalled that the result of monetary policy allowed Uruguay to reduce its cost of financing in international markets in the last year. The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, explained that the consolidation of low levels of inflation represents a key aspect for the country's long-term growth. Labat spoke on Wednesday, September 6, at the XI National Congress of Graduates in Economic Sciences organized by the College of Accountants, Economists and Administrators of Uruguay (CCEAU). Consolidating low inflation would allow, among other things, companies to operate with smaller inventories and access better credit conditions to grow, which would boost the expansion of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP), said the president of the BCU. In this sense, economist Diego Labat defended this strategic approach of the Central Bank which, he said, is far from representing an arbitrary idea: "This is not a whim, Uruguay has historically low growth rates and, if we want to reverse them, we need companies that take other risks, that can grow in a different way. And for that we need lower inflation," he said. The president of the Central Bank defended the management of monetary policy, which from the reduction of inflation, allowed the interest rate to be lowered and, as a consequence, allows Uruguay to reduce its cost of financing in international financial markets. "Today investors are demanding from Uruguay a rate of 250 basis points less than a year ago. That is a saving in the issuance of debt and any investment project will have a lower financial cost. Are we happy? No. We would like the rate to be lower and we understand that (by validating lower rates) the market expects inflation to continue to fall," Labat concluded.
