Title: The XII Conference on Central Bank Law began
text: October 24, 2023 The XII Conference on Law Ban cocentra list began The opening was in charge of the president of the BCU, Diego Labat This morning began the XII Conference on Central Bank Law, an annual event that brings together professionals and academics at the national and regional levels. The opening of the Conference was in charge of the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, who welcomed and thanked the exhibitors and the public attending the meeting. Labat highlighted the relevance of the aspects that will be discussed during the two days of activity: notarial issues, social security reform, stock market, payment system, innovation and open finance. Regarding the social security reform, he stressed that the Conferences address the changes of said reform that affect the role of the BCU. Regarding the payment system, he highlighted the strong focus with which the BCU works on the issue: "The Bank has a central project, the Fast Payment System, which is a system that has been operating since the beginning of 2021 and that, step by step, has been gaining strength." He stressed that it is the system that allows instant transfers every day, which began operating 24/7 in June and that "it will continue to have improvements in the coming months." In the same sense, he stressed that next year it will be possible to pay through QR code, which "generates challenges also from a legal point of view." On the other hand, on the subject of innovation, he indicated that the Bank is having an important agenda and, regarding open finance, he said that "in the coming years it will be very strong" and that it generates enormous challenges for the BCU. Following the opening of the president of the BCU, the day's presentations began, organized into three thematic tables. The first table addressed notarial issues related to the central bank's activity. The notary Maria Paola Bagnoli offered a summary of the notarial documentation required to be presented to the Notarial Department of the BCU, addressing frequent queries. Subsequently, Guillermo Contreras addressed the new regime of access to the affidavits submitted to the BCU in compliance with Laws 18,930 and 19,484, after the modifications introduced by Law 20,018. The third presentation was given by Ines Cobas (Internal Audit of the Nation) who explored the modifications in the regulations related to ownership and the final beneficiary. The second table focused on the reform of social security and its impact on the BCU's competencies. Rodolfo Saldain, PhD specialized in Labor Law and Social Security, who chaired the Commission of Experts and the drafting team of the Law 20.130 of the Social Security Reform, analyzed constitutive aspects and the novelties of the reform. Next, the manager of Legal Advice of the BCU, Daniel Artecona, addressed the impact that the new law has generated on the Pension Savings Fund Administrators (AFAPs). The third and last table of the day was called the Stock Market and was made up of two professionals from the BCU. Dr. Mariana Irazoqui presented a compilation of the most frequent observations made to trust agreements, while Dr. Alejandra Rodriguez analyzed the civil liability of senior personnel in securities intermediaries in liquidation. The second day of the Central Bank Law Conference will take place on Wednesday, October 25.

Title: Diego Labat at the Meeting of Central Bank Governors of Latin America and the Caribbean
text: November 08, 2023 Diego Labat at the Meeting of Central Bank Presidents of Latin America and the Caribbean The president of the BCU spoke about the challenges and opportunities of monetary policy The President of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, is participating in the 58th Meeting of the Network of Chief Economists of Central Banks and Ministries of Finance of Latin America and the Caribbean, which takes place from November 7 to 9 at the headquarters of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) in Washington D.C. United States, in hybrid format. The meeting includes public sessions with panel discussions with finance ministers and central bank governors from the region and two research and policy seminars. This morning, November 8, Labat spoke (virtually from Montevideo) about the challenges and opportunities of monetary policy in the current global context during a discussion with central bank governors from Latin America and the Caribbean. The panel was made up of the president of the Central Bank of Costa Rica, Roger Madrigal Lopez; the President of the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago, Alvin Hilaire; and the president of the Central Bank of Peru, Julio Velarde Flores. In that instance, economist Labat highlighted the importance of the implementation of inflation targeting regimes in several countries in the region as a tool that made it possible to face the international context of high prices starting in 2020. Regarding Uruguay, the president of the BCU said that the country had a historical average inflation of around 8% over the last 15 years, which is why the current Board of Directors considered the construction of a robust inflation targeting regime with the proposal to move towards a quality currency. To do this, it was based on four basic pillars: the commitment to lower inflation as the sole objective of monetary policy; the interest rate as an instrument; the strengthening of monetary policy communication; and a free-floating exchange rate regime. He then told how the process developed from 2020 to the present, where inflation has been near the center of the target range for five months. He added that the inflation targeting regime in Uruguay is a regime "under construction", where the expectations of agents have been reduced, but its convergence within the range is still pending.

Title: Diego Labat spoke at the "CUTI Business Forum 2023" meeting, organized by the Uruguayan Chamber of Information Technologies
text: November 10, 2023 Diego Labat spoke at the "CUTI Business Forum 2023" meeting, organized by the Uruguayan Chamber of Information Technologies The president of the BCU spoke about collaboration and regulation in an environment of innovation and disruption in the fintech ecosystem The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, stressed the importance of having a regulation of the financial system in Uruguay that generates "a level playing field" to contribute to the collaborative development of the industry. Labat spoke this Thursday, November 8, at the "CUTI Business Forum 2023" meeting, which brought together business leaders, entrepreneurs, and analysts from the information technology ecosystem, at the event center of the Technological Laboratory of Uruguay (LATU) in Montevideo. In his speech, the president of the BCU reflected that the perception of a supposed opposition between the role of banks and fintech companies has currently changed: "Today it is clear that we are moving towards collaboration, where each one will occupy their place and their role, with an increasingly collaborative environment." In this sense, Labat stressed the importance of having rules of the game that allow the development of the entire industry. "There will be those who are successful and those who are not, but it is important to have a level ground, with ease of entry and without barriers," he said. On the other hand, Labat stressed that financial companies today have the ability to share functions: "A bank or a fintech does not necessarily fulfill all functions. You have to see each player and, from there, start to regulate." The president of the BCU said that the stability of the Uruguayan financial system represents a good starting point for innovation: "Sometimes stability is seen as opposed to development. And I say that in Uruguay there is room to develop the financial system while maintaining that well-earned solidity." To this end, the BCU seeks to "give guides and signals on where regulation is going, so that the private sector finds the places (to innovate and develop). The role of the Central Bank is to facilitate, to level the playing field, to promote and motivate the actors," concluded Labat. On the panel, the president of the BCU was accompanied by the director of Mercado Libre, Osvaldo Gimenez; the advisor in Strategic and Legal Projects of dLocal, Nadia Yavitz; and the secretary general of the Uruguayan Chamber of Information Technologies (CUTI), Amilcar Perea.

Para ello, el BCU busca dar guas y seales sobre hacia dnde va la regulacin, para que el sector privado encuentre los lugares (para innovar y desarrollarse). Title: The BCU held the Financial Innovation Meeting with broad participation of members of the financial system
text: The BCU held the Financial Innovation Meeting with broad participation of members of the financial system Diego Labat inaugurated the event that addressed the results of the innovation roundtables and the prospects for the future of the country's financial innovation ecosystem CENTRAL BANK OF THE URU( Alfredo Alio, manager of Management and Strategic Planning of the BCU; Ana Claudia de los Heros, manager of the Payment System and Patricia Tudisco, intendant of Financial Regulation of the BCU. This Wednesday, in the Enrique Iglesias Room of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), the "Financial Innovation Meeting - Results of the tables and perspectives for the future" was held, which brought together members of the country's financial innovation ecosystem with the aim of exchanging on what has been done this year, sharing the results of the innovation tables developed with the impetus of the BCU, and outline some work prospects for the coming year. The welcome was given by the president of the BCU, economist Diego Labat, who celebrated the attendance of the audience, who filled the auditorium to a full house, and thanked the Bank staff who, since 2020, have been working in the orbit of the innovation program promoted by the institution, NOVA BCU. And he highlighted, with respect to the conformation of the workspaces, the importance of the proactive role of each of the people who make up the innovation program at all levels, both from the Node, the Observatory and the Innovation Office created in the BCU. "Today central banks have a more proactive role than we had before and we have to fulfill that role of proposing, motivating, pushing and doing; but this requires that there be a response from the other side." He also pointed out actions that confirm this synergy between the parts that make up the country's financial innovation ecosystem: "In this year 2023 there were very important changes, such as the fact that the working groups were led by the industry and not by the Bank, but the tasks do not end there, we believe that we have to continue." He added that "from the BCU we intend to create a sense of community among all parties, because clearly there are things that can be achieved with collaboration." In this same sense, Labat insisted that in order to continue moving forward it is necessary "that we work on a level ground, that is to say that it has to be a space in which those who are already there appear, new players appear, the regulated and the unregulated appear. We know that there are technologies that are already imposed, but we also have to give space to technologies that are not yet imposed but we know that they exist." Labat stressed that, although much remains to be done, the BCU values the achievements made very positively, through strong work from all parties that make the innovation program possible. At the closing of the activity, Ana Claudia de los Heros, manager of the Payment System, referred to innovation from the perspective of the BCU. He spoke of the transversal work and the formation of the Innovation Observatory, which has made it possible to monitor what was happening in the market and in the industry. He mentioned that when talking about innovation, it must first be recognized that it exists and referred to five verbs that, he understands, contribute to its description: "innovate" (what it means for the BCU and its promotion in the financial system); "collaborate" (the importance of creating a collaborative community); "understanding" (market effects, risks and ways to mitigate them); "viability" (innovation by making tools available to make it work); and "adapt" (regulations and laws and the institutional level so that innovation is developed). For her part, Patricia Tudisco, intendant of Financial Regulation of the BCU, mentioned that in all this work it has helped "to be an open-door bank", that the industry is there and "that we can listen". He spoke of the lynchings about the work carried out and in which work will continue and for this he commented on some specific tasks such as those carried out in the Digital Onboarding Table, which focused on the issue of money laundering; in Virtual Assets, where work is being done in a consultancy with the World Bank; and on the issue of collective financing platforms, where "there is room for improvement" and this "will be worked on next year"; as well as in Open Finance, where "intense work continues". Finally, Alfredo Alio, manager of Management and Strategic Planning of the BCU, mentioned that the result of the work carried out by the Office of Innovation and the Observatory has been "of a high level". He said that the mission is to facilitate the space to enable common work and indicated that the Bank will facilitate and seek consensus on these issues, without ceasing to regulate and supervise. He thanked in general all the sectors of the Bank involved in the theme and in the organization of the event, as well as the exhibitors and all the public present.

Title: Pilar Gonzlez received the award of the twenty-seventh edition of the Figari Prize
text: Pilar Gonzalez received the award of the twenty-seventh edition of the Figari Prize The ceremony, held on December 20 at the Figari Museum, was attended by the president of the BCU, Diego Labat On Wednesday, December 20, the Figari Award, the highest national distinction for the career of an active plastic artist, was awarded to Pilar Gonzalez and the retrospective exhibition of her work was inaugurated at the Figari Museum by the curatorship of oscar Larroca. The ceremony was attended by the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, the Minister of Education and Culture (MEC), Pablo Da Silveira; the National Director of Culture, Mariana Wainstein and the Director of the Figari Museum, Pablo Thiago Rocca. Economist Diego Labat recalled that the Figari Prize was instituted in 1995 by the BCU: "It is really a pride for Uruguay to have been able to make this contribution to culture and art since that date. It is a contribution to artists in life, to recognize the trajectory of those artists (...) because those artists in some way are the basis for culture to continue to be renewed." Labat expressed his wish that "this virtuous spiral continues" and "we will have for many years and for a long time to come, this delivery of the Figari Prize." He also thanked the work of all those who made this instance possible: "Clearly there is a very strong work of the Museum team, with Pablo at the head, but also the entire MEC team, the National Directorate of Culture, the cultural management team of the Central Bank. It is a joint effort to get to today." The president of the BCU expressed his recognition to Pilar Gonzalez and said that the applause that was felt at the beginning of the event "was worth a thousand words." Finally, he congratulated the artist and expressed his desire for her to receive more awards and recognition. He also recalled that each award-winning work remains in the Bank and pointed out that one of the efforts that is intended to be made is that the collection that the Bank owns travels the national territory: "Luckily, both in 2022 and in 2023 we have held exhibitions in several cities. Now we are going to start, as soon as the year begins, with a new exhibition; the idea is precisely that these works are shown, that these works have other accessibility," he concluded. The jury of the XXVII edition of the award, made up of Domingo Ferreira, Maria Frick and Elisa Perez Buchelli, unanimously decided to award the distinction. In the ruling, the court justifies the award with the following words: "Pilar Gonzalez is an artist with an outstanding and constant career for more than four decades, and her own and consolidated plastic language. She was a student of teachers Eduardo Fornasari and Nelson Ramos. He worked as a teacher, illustrator in the press and in the publishing field. She also worked in curatorship and museum management. She has worked in the theatrical field as a costume and set designer. He has received numerous recognitions and distinctions. His work is characterized by the intensity of his expressive language and exploration in various artistic media." Pilar Gonzalez was born in Montevideo on November 24, 1955. He trained with prestigious teachers in the 1970s and 1980s. His drawings, paintings and installations have been distinguished with various awards and have been exhibited in solo and group exhibitions in America, Europe and Australia.

Title: Experts analyzed risks, challenges and opportunities for the Uruguayan economy
text: Experts analyzed "risks, challenges and opportunities for the Uruguayan economy" The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara, analyzed together with experts from multilateral organizations the current scenario of the national economy in the framework of a conference organized by the Uruguayan-German Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Tower 4 of the Word Trade Center in Montevideo. For Bergara "geopolitics is plagued by uncertainties, which in turn generate risks and opportunities." "With the actions of the BCU we try to give stability to a fundamental variable such as the exchange rate. We seek to give signs of confidence in both directions, to exporters and citizens in general," he added. He argued that the attempts made by the Uruguayan government to ease the turbulence and maintain macroeconomic order are perceived by risk rating agencies, multilateral credit agencies and the Investors. Institutional quality, legal certainty and macroeconomic stability constitute the support to face the growing uncertainties, added to the fact that "there has been a fruitful learning in the management of turbulence" , he said. In this context, he pointed out that the Uruguayan economy continues to grow from domestic demand, exports and a consistent surplus of the current account of the balance of payments. Among the challenges, he established the need to reactivate the investment process, transfer growth to improvements in employment levels, generate a downward trajectory of the fiscal deficit and solve some sectoral problems of profitability. In turn, Bergara referred to the technological dynamics that also generate uncertainty and drastically changed the logics of business, tax and labor relations. "We see the technological impact every day and Uruguay has the bases to take advantage of the opportunities that are generated in this world," he said. The panel of experts that participated in this morning's meeting also included the participation of the resident representative in Uruguay of the World Bank (WB), Matilde Bordon; the representative of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), Morgan Doyle; and the director representative of the Development Bank of Latin America  CAF, German Rios. Title: Speech at a fintech forum: The central bank's approach is proactive and constructive at the same time
text: June 26, 2019 BCU President at fintech forum: "The Central Bank's approach is both proactive and constructive" The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Alberto Grana, reviewed the opportunities and challenges that the emergence of technological innovations applied to the financial business implies for the financial system and citizens in general. Grana participated as a guest speaker at the Montevideo Fintech Forum that takes place between Wednesday and Thursday in Montevideo with the presence of government authorities and companies in the sector. During the presentation called "Fintechs: challenges and opportunities for central banks (/Communications/Conferences/Grana_Foro_Fintech_20190626.pdf) ", the president of the BCU referred to the opportunities it presents at the moment for example to reduce market inefficiencies, the innovative use of information for risk management, the increase in competition as well as the use of technology for regulation and supervision. He also stated that for users it implies benefits such as financial inclusion, obtaining better and more adequate financial services, lower transaction costs and more efficient services. However, the president of the Central Bank recalled that this process is not without challenges, in particular regarding cybersecurity, information privacy and the prevention of money laundering and financing of terrorism, aspects that must be taken into account in account to preserve the good international reputation of the country. "The Uruguayan financial system enjoys a great international reputation, evaluated from different perspectives in terms of solidity, stability, solvency and its methodology for preventing money laundering and financing terrorism," he recalled. This aspect is relevant in the opinion of the president of the BCU: "There we have a challenge given that, in the hurry, sometimes excellent business ideas have to be compatible with the analysis of the type of risk that derives from it," he said. "The best thing that can happen to a fintech in Uruguay or in the world is that there is a regulator that takes into account the type of risk that is generated and how to mitigate it. The irruption, in a good way, of an alternative model, can contribute to efficiency gains and greater well-being of citizens, but it implies taking care of the risks and that is the responsibility of the Central Bank. The central bank's approach is both proactive and constructive," he said. The day before, President Alberto Grana also presented at a round table within the framework of the Digital Economy Conference organized by the Association of Computer Scientists of Uruguay. During that instance, he referred among other aspects to the successful pilot experience of digital banknote -e-peso- that the BCU developed during 2018. He pointed out that in the course of 2019 the Central Bank of Uruguay is working in transversal teams in the analysis of the scope and the roadmap of the e-peso project.

Title: Speech at ACDE: Promoting the stock market is a central objective
text: December 6, 2016 Mario Bergara at ACDE: "Boosting the stock market is a central objective" The regulations that allow a simplified issuance in the stock market for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) were put into consultation with the aim of making it possible to finance relevant projects, announced the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara. The hierarch, who presented together with the government economic team at the Forum of the Christian Association of Business Leaders (ACDE), recalled that the simplification of the emission regulations will allow the participation of MSMEs, since it reduces the costs of assembling the process. "The scheme exempts these types of companies from some obligations that they do not have to have and it makes it possible for them to go to the stock market to seek financing," Bergara said. In that sense, he exemplified that he will not be required to have independent directors, to make a semi-annual limited audit review report and to have an Audit and Oversight Committee. Also, from the documentary point of view, the BCU will offer model contracts and emission prospectuses that facilitate the process. "Enhancing the stock market is a central objective in the central bank's policy in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance; the intention is to make it possible to finance relevant projects in the same way as happened with some infrastructure projects that seek to channel retail savings," said the hierarch. In the same way, he recalled that the "regulation in the capital market aims to protect the unsophisticated investor." On the other hand, Bergara pointed to the importance of understanding the phenomenon of electronic platforms aimed at the financial system, which are more complex than those used for example in transport. "You have to understand what each one does to evaluate what degree of effective competition they have with traditional financial intermediation (...) be attentive if there is something to protect and take into account the possible impacts of a systemic nature," he said. In the opinion of the president of the Central Bank, these platforms reduce the asymmetry of information, which reduces the profitability potential of traditional financial intermediation. However, he said that banks have had the capacity to adapt for two thousand years and, therefore, will surely adapt to generate hybrid mechanisms that allow them to compete with these new modalities. "We have to understand well what is the object to protect from the regulatory point of view and based on that advance in a regulation that levels the forms of competences of all financial institutions in a positive way, because more competition is positive," he said. Finally , during his presentation at ACDE Bergara, he reflected on the importance of strengthening the regulatory framework in the insurance market to preserve the savings of workers who retire through the Pension Savings Fund Administrators (AFAP). What is bought at the time of retirement is a pension income, which must take into account survival, the possibility of a second person gaining passivity and what profitability it should have. These aspects, known as mortality tables, will be considered shortly by Banco Centra with information from the Social Security Bank. In that sense, Bergara said that "the new mortality tables must be dynamic so that 20 years do not pass without adapting." It is not the Central Bank that must set the parameters of social security, but a rate to require technical reserves from insurance companies, so "a methodology will be considered in such a way that this rate moves with variables observable in the market," he added. The proposed changes will help to give more transparency, to adapt to reality these parameters of capitalization of social security with data from reality and to solve the sustainability of this pillar for the future. Likewise, Bergara announced the consultation of a new regulation that implies transparency of information (prices and costs) of insurance companies so that workers who retire can choose between one or the other. "We need to protect the fund from the passivities of the workers also through the other pillar of the system that is the insurance companies," summarized the president of the BCU. During his presentation at the ACDE Forum, Mario Bergara, also reviewed the context of volatility and global uncertainty that is deepened by some specific events of a political nature. In this scenario, he pointed out that monetary policy will continue to be contractionary through the management of monetary aggregates and the issuance of Monetary Regulation Bills. In that sense, Bergara dismissed that "the evolution of interest rates puts downward pressure on the exchange rate, since in general they evolve in the same direction." "Today the exchange rate is driven primarily by global financial conditions and therefore by the expectations of global agents," he emphasized. The ACDE forum called "More inclusion, more innovation, better insertion: economic policy in the face of new challenges" had the participation of Bergara together with the Minister of Economy and Finance, Danilo Astori, the undersecretary of the MEF Pablo Ferreri; the director of the Macroeconomic Advisory of the MEF, Andres Masoller; and the director of the Office of Planning and Budget, alvaro Garcia. Necesitamos proteger el fondo de las pasividades de los trabajadores tambin mediante el otro pilar del sistema que son las empresas de seguros, resumi el presidente del BCU. En este escenario, seal que la poltica monetaria seguir siendo contractiva mediante la gestin de agregados monetarios y la emisin de Letras de Regulacin Monetaria. En ese sentido, Bergara desestim que la evolucin de las tasas de inters presione a la baja al tipo de cambio, ya que en general evolucionan en la misma direccin. Hoy el tipo de cambio se mueve primordialmente por las condiciones financieras globales y por tanto con las expectativas de los agentes globales, enfatiz. El foro de ACDE denominado "Ms inclusin, ms innovacin, mejor insercin: la poltica econmica frente a los nuevo desafos" tuvo la participacin de Bergara junto al ministro de Economa y Finanzas, Danilo Astori, el subsecretario del MEF Pablo Ferreri; el director de la Asesora Macroeconmica del MEF, Andrs Masoller; y el director de la Oficina d Planeamiento y Presupuesto, lvaro Garca. Title: Speech about the situation in the ACDE economic forum
text: December 19, 2019 The president of the BCU spoke about the situation at the ACDE economic forum The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Alberto Gra96a, spoke on Thursday, December 19, at the Economic Forum of the Christian Association of Business Leaders (ACDE). The conference reviewed several aspects related to the Central Bank, in particular from the challenging international environment that has manifested itself in recent years. From that starting point, Gra96a referred to monetary-exchange rate policy, inflationary dynamics, financial stability and pending challenges. The president's reflections began from the global context where he argued that the trade war between China and the US has caused a persistent decline in global growth expectations, while the continuous announcements about the trade war also determined high global volatility, both in the dollar and in the financial markets. Likewise, the regional environment is marked by high uncertainty with multiple risks in Argentina, where a very significant deterioration in economic and financial conditions was observed, as well as in Brazil, which has had ups and downs along with low growth rates and recent episodes of volatility that forced the Central Bank of Brazil to intervene in the foreign exchange market. Added to this is the situation in Chile, where after social instability, the Central Bank of Chile also had to intervene in the face of strong pressures on the exchange rate. In this challenging global and regional scenario, the president of the Central Bank stressed that the markets' perception of Uruguay is positive, which is reflected in a stable sovereign risk premium in line with other investment-grade countries in Latin America. The international and regional context had important impacts on the foreign exchange market, in particular, due to the rapid currency change in the portfolios managed by pension funds. In this sense, the magnitude of the funds involved motivated the intervention of the BCU in order to avoid sudden movements in the exchange rate, recalled economist Alberto Gra96a. "The interventions made it possible to process an adjustment of the exchange rate without high volatility events, particularly in comparison with the main countries of the region as well as with countries that compete with our products and markets," he said in his presentation. This was possible because the accumulation of reserves in the period 2009-2014 and in 2017 as a result of the purchases of foreign currency in the foreign exchange market allowed a countercyclical management of the BCU's balance sheet, he said. Gra96a recalled that interventions in the foreign exchange market generate mirror impacts on the stock of Monetary Regulation Bills (LRM) and on the Central Bank's deficit. In this regard, he stressed that the current sales cycle contributes to reducing the parafiscal deficit. "In this context, there is still no relevant pass-through from exchange rate to prices, nor second-round effects on the rest of prices," Gra96a said. He added that monetary policy has maintained a moderately contractionary character, consistent with the current phase of the economic cycle, which has also been reflected in the recent evolution of the rates of bills. Among the challenges ahead, he highlighted as relevant to continue the process of de-dollarization as a long-term policy; to continue progress in the development of domestic markets in local currency; the construction of the exchange rate futures market; the development of the e-Peso project and the monitoring of the development of finTechs; as well as to contribute to the discussion of financial aspects to the reform of the pension system.

A esto se aade la situacin de Chile, donde luego de la inestabilidad social, el Banco Central de Chile tambin tuvo que intervenir ante fuertes presiones sobre el tipo de cambio. En este escenario global y regional desafiante, el presidente del Banco Central resalt que la percepcin de los mercados sobre Uruguay es positiva, lo que se refleja en una prima por riesgo soberano estable en lnea con otros pases con grado inversor en Amrica Latina. El contexto internacional y regional tuvo impactos importantes en el mercado de cambios, en particular, por el rpido cambio de moneda en los portafolios administrados por los fondos de pensin. En ese sentido, la magnitud de los fondos involucrados motiv la intervencin del BCU a efectos de evitar movimientos bruscos en el tipo de cambio, record el economista Alberto Graa. Las intervenciones permitieron procesar un ajuste del tipo de cambio sin eventos de alta volatilidad, en particular en comparacin con los principales pases de la regin as como con pases competidores de nuestros productos y mercados, sostuvo en su presentacin. Esto fue posible debido a que la acumulacin de reservas en el periodo 2009-2014 y en 2017 fruto de las compras de divisas en el mercado de cambios permiti un manejo anticclico de la hoja de balance del BCU, dijo. Graa record que las intervenciones en el mercado de cambio generan impactos en espejo en el stock de Letras de Regulacin Monetaria (LRM) y en el dficit del Banco Central. En este aspecto resalt que el actual ciclo de ventas contribuye a reducir el dficit parafiscal. En este contexto, an no se observa un traspaso relevante de tipo de cambio a precios, ni efectos de segunda vuelta sobre el resto de los precios, dijo Graa. Aadi que la poltica monetaria ha mantenido un carcter moderadamente contractivo, consistente con la actual fase del ciclo econmico lo que tambin se ha reflejado en la evolucin reciente de las tasas de las Letras. Entre los desafos a futuro, destac como relevante continuar el proceso de desdolarizacin como poltica de largo plazo; proseguir los avances en el desarrollo de los mercados domsticos en moneda local; la construccin del mercado de futuros del tipo de cambio; el desarrollo del proyecto de e-Peso y el monitoreo del desarrollo de las finTech; as como aportar la discusin de aspectos financieros a la reforma del sistema de pensiones. Title: Speech on the anniversary of BEVSA: It is necessary to continue betting on the development and deepening of the capital market
text: September 6, 2019 Alberto Graf1a on BEVSA's anniversary: "It is necessary to continue betting on the development and deepening of the capital market " The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Alberto Graf1a, participated in a meeting that took place this Thursday, September 5, for the 25th anniversary of the Electronic Stock Exchange of Uruguay S.A. (BEVSA). On the occasion, Graf1a highlighted the importance of BEVSA in generating information for the markets, with products such as the Price Vector and the indices that measure the premium by country risk. Likewise, the president of the Central Bank said that the work between the monetary authority and financial agents is aimed at deepening the derivatives markets, such as exchange rate futures, a very important element for the development perspective of the capital market. "Uruguay needs to deepen and develop its capital market and obviously it is a very important fact that resident and non-resident agents can have hedging instruments available. in a deep and transparent market," Graf1a added. In that sense, exchange rate futures are a very important element for the development prospects of the capital market. Part of that path began with the increase in demand for exchange hedging that has already existed in the context of global volatility, he recalled. On the other hand, the president of the BCU emphasized the possibility that exists for the integration of new technologies with the financial system, giving as an example the future insertion of the digital ticket in the Payment System. "This calls us to work with different actors around this product to which we bet from a perspective of efficiency gain, cost reduction and security of the payment system , in particular for the retailers," said the president of the Central Bank. In that sense, he stressed that this year studies and research are being carried out to define how this product will be inserted in an ecosystem in which they already coexist. issuers of electronic money and modalities based on mobile telephony, among others. Graf1a also said that "the digital banknote project does not replace the real gross settlement system of the Central Bank." BEVSA began operations on September 5, 1994 with 26 public and private financial institutions to generate a scope for negotiation and settlement of financial transactions. Among its partners and special partners are the local banks, the Pension Fund Administrators (AFAPs), the Parastatal Funds, the Insurance Bank, and the BCU. In BEVSA the Exchange, Money and Securities Markets are operated.

Title: There are opportunities to take advantage of and risks to mitigate
text: September 6, 2019 Alberto Graf1a: "There are opportunities to take advantage of and risks to mitigate" The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Alberto Graf1a, held a conference yesterday on regulation in Blockchain and Fintech within the framework of the second edition of the international event Blockchain Summit Uruguay. Graf1a highlighted as positive the technological development which he also characterized as a "reasonable, dynamic and at the same time risky" process. With regard to the so-called fintech, in his presentation he focused on financing and the payment system, referring in the case of the first, to the modality of loans (known as "peer to peer lending") and crowdfunding, a crowdfunding mechanism. Among the most immediate regulatory aspects of our country, he mentioned in relation to the modality of loans, that there is a regulation issued in 2018 by the Superintendence of Financial Services of the BCU. On crowdfunding, he pointed out that there is a bill under consideration in Parliament on entrepreneurship and that regulates certain aspects of the financing mechanism. "The regulation of fintech has been the focus of analysis both by academia and by central banks around the world," Graf1a added. For the president of the BCU, the most indicated is a "regulatory approach based on risks" but that allows taking advantage of the opportunities of this new system, such as contributing to breaking down entry barriers, reducing costs of transaction, gain in efficiency, faster business , among others. "The best thing that can happen to the ecosystem is to have an attentive regulator that allows a healthy development of the system," Graf1a said. He stressed that the principles that should govern regulation are, among others, functionality and proportionality. On the other hand, with regard to the payment system, Graf1a emphasized that "we are witnessing a true digital revolution and that the BCU will continue working for a Increasingly efficient payment system." In another order, he referred to the recent and successful digital banknote pilot project developed by the BCU, which occurred "taking advantage of technological progress and the increase in the use of mobile telephony". In this regard, he warned that the BCU will break into a payment system where there are already issuers of electronic money and other payment methods , therefore it is evaluating The way of insertion of the digital ticket in the ecosystem.

Por otro lado, en lo que respecta al sistema de pagos, Graa enfatiz en que estamos asistiendo a una verdadera revolucin digital y que el BCU seguir trabajando por un sistema de pagos cada vez ms eficiente. Title: In this turbulent environment, Uruguay has financial strengths
text: April 5, 2019 Alberto Grana: "In this turbulent environment, Uruguay has financial strengths" The Meeting Line cycle organized by Somos Uruguay at the Sheraton Montevideo Hotel counted last Tuesday with the presentation of the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Alberto Grana. The dissertation was entitled "Uruguay in the global and regional context". The president of the BCU explained that the global economic situation is characterized by a slowdown in the main economies and a growing weight of geopolitical factors in the global business climate (trade war between the US and China, Brexit, etc.). In that sense, Grana pointed out that Uruguay is no stranger to this situation. At the same time, the regional environment presents, according to Grana, "a very complex scenario". With regard to Argentina, he remarked that "there have been sharp falls in the level of activity in the context of the macroeconomic crisis" suffered by that country since last year. In the case of Brazil, he said that "low annual growth rates have been verified in recent years, with periods in which it has technically been in economic recession." Grana referred to some of the main macroeconomic variables in both countries, which certainly do not present a very auspicious scenario, mainly in the case of Argentina. He added that in the case of the northern country, the recent refusal of Congress to promote a reform of the pension system sought by the Brazilian economic authorities, "opens a mantle of uncertainty given the situation of public finances in that country." However, for Grana "in this turbulent environment, Uruguay has financial strengths." He explained that the increase in reserves for a few years to this part has been mainly due to interventions by the BCU in the exchange market, in order "to avoid an undue appreciation of the peso against the dollar", in a context in which until not long ago as a result of the financial crisis of 2008-2009 and the expansionary monetary policies in the US and Europe there was an important flows to emerging countries, including Uruguay. He affirmed that the effort of the acquisition of foreign currency "has been justified and if it is necessary to do so, it will be justified again", by virtue of the attention to the real sector of the economy and the contribution that the BCU must do through price stability to economic growth. Grana also referred to the slowdown in economic activity in our country in recent quarters, which together with the fight against inflation should mark the responses of monetary policy of the BCU. He also argued that the deterioration of the labor market is a reflection of the economic slowdown. In relation to monetary policy, he stressed that it will remain "moderately contractionary", which makes clear the importance that the BCU attaches to it in this phase of the cycle. to the level of economic activity. With regard to the exchange rate, he stressed that "it has continued its evolution at a global level", and that with respect to Uruguay's main competitors by markets in the world the Real exchange rate is at reasonable levels. The president of the BCU also took the opportunity to mention that the BCU is the first public body with institutional certification of all its processes under the same quality management system (ISO 9001: 2015 by LSQA S.A and Quality Austria). Finally, he announced some of the Bank's strategic initiatives planned for 2019 , among which the evaluation of Fintech stands out, with the aim of "generating adequate regulation that allows mitigating risks, but also allow the growth space of something that is here to stay." La disertacin se titul Uruguay en el contexto global y regional. El presidente del BCU explic que la situacin econmica global se caracteriza por una desaceleracin de las principales economas y un creciente peso de factores geopolticos en el clima de negocios global (guerra comercial entre EEUU y China, Brexit, etc.). En ese sentido, Graa seal que Uruguay no est ajeno a esta situacin. A su vez el entorno regional presenta, segn Graa, un escenario muy complejo. En lo que refiere a la Argentina, remarc que ha habido bruscas cadas del nivel de actividad en el marco de la crisis macroeconmica que sufre ese pas desde el ao pasado. En el caso de Brasil, sostuvo que se viene verificando en los ltimos aos tasas de crecimiento anuales bajas, con perodos en los que ha estado tcnicamente en recesin econmica. Graa hizo referencia a algunas de las principales variables macroeconmicas en ambos pases, que por cierto no presentan un escenario muy auspicioso, fundamentalmente en el caso de la Argentina. Aadi que en el caso del pas norteo la reciente negativa del Congreso a impulsar una reforma del sistema previsional pretendida por las autoridades econmicas brasileas, abre un manto de incertidumbre dada la situacin de las finanzas pblicas en ese pas. No obstante, para Graa en este entorno turbulento, Uruguay cuenta con fortalezas financieras. Explic que el incremento de las reservas de unos cuantos aos a esta parte se ha debido principalmente a intervenciones del BCU en el mercado de cambios, a efectos de evitar una indebida apreciacin del peso frente al dlar, en un contexto en el que hasta no hace mucho a raz de la crisis financiera de 2008-2009 y las polticas monetarias expansivas en EEUU y Europa hubo importante flujos hacia los pases emergentes, incluido Uruguay. Afirm que el esfuerzo de la adquisicin de divisas ha sido justificado y de ser necesario hacerlo, ser nuevamente justificado, en virtud de la atencin al sector real de la economa y la contribucin que el BCU debe hacer a travs de la estabilidad de precios al crecimiento econmico. Graa se refiri tambin a la desaceleracin de la actividad econmica de nuestro pas en los ltimos trimestres, que junto al combate a la inflacin debe marcar las respuestas de poltica monetaria del BCU. Asimismo, sostuvo que el deterioro del mercado laboral es el reflejo de la desaceleracin econmica. En relacin a la poltica monetaria, destac que se mantendr moderadamente contractiva, lo que deja en claro la importancia que el BCU le otorga en esta fase del ciclo al nivel de actividad econmica. En lo que refiere al tipo de cambio destac que ha seguido su evolucin a nivel global, y que respecto de los principales competidores de Uruguay por mercados en el mundo el tipo de cambio real se encuentra a niveles razonables. El presidente del BCU aprovech la ocasin tambin para mencionar que el BCU es el primer organismo pblico con certificacin institucional de todos sus procesos bajo un mismo sistema de gestin de calidad (Norma ISO 9001:2015 por parte de LSQA S.A y Quality Austria). Por ltimo, anunci algunas de las iniciativas estratgicas del Banco previstas para 2019, entre las cuales se destaca la evaluacin de las Fintech, con el objetivo de generar una regulacin adecuada que permita mitigar riesgos, pero tambin permitir el espacio de crecimiento de algo que lleg para quedarse. Title: It is appropriate for the exchange rate to follow global trends and float freely, but not abrupt jumps
text: May 29, 2019 Alberto Graf1a: "It is appropriate that the exchange rate follows global trends and there is free floating, but not abrupt jumps" In the cycle of Working Lunches organized by the Association of Marketing Leaders (ADM) presented this Wednesday, May 29, the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Alberto Graf1a. The dissertation was entitled "The Central Bank of Uruguay facing the challenges of the global, regional and domestic situation" (/Communications/Conferences/Presentation%20Alberto%20Graf1a_ADM_290519.pdf) . The president of the BCU began by explaining that "we are in a complex global context" and that "political uncertainty is not a good advisor for business." In relation to the global situation, he referred to the trade war between the US and China, describing a reciprocal imposition of tariffs and its main global repercussions, among others. which he highlighted: cracks in the architecture of international trade, postponed investment decisions, difficulties in value and supplier chains, and an increase in risk aversion . For Graf1a, all these repercussions imply a lower growth of the global economy, "with constant downward revisions". With regard to the region, Graf1a emphasized the fall in activity and the prospects for moderate growth not only for Brazil and Argentina, but also for the rest of the countries of Latin America. He pointed out the macroeconomic imbalances that Argentina was going through in particular. "The global and regional economic cycle is transmitted to Uruguay," Graf1a said. He added that "the economic slowdown of our main trading partners has contributed to the slowdown of economic activity in Uruguay." In another order, he ratified the monetary policy, on which he maintained that "it maintains a contractionary bias appropriate to the phase of the economic cycle." The president of the BCU also referred to the evolution of the exchange rate. "To think that the evolution of the exchange rate only depends on depreciating the Uruguayan peso at the pace of Argentina , which is in crisis, is a serious and profound mistake," he said. "It is appropriate that the exchange rate follows global trends and there is free floating, but not abrupt jumps," he emphasized. He warned that "sudden changes in the exchange rate generate volatility and uncertainty in the calculation of the profitability of economic agents," and that this has been the reason why the BCU intervenes in the market, always under a counter-cyclical logic. Graf1a gave an account of the level of reserves that allows the bank to carry out the aforementioned operations. "Stress tests show that the level of reserves would remain adequate even in hypothetical adverse scenarios," he added. In another passage of his presentation, he stated that "competitiveness does not depend only on the exchange rate, since the rise in the exchange rate has its correlate in the rate of inflation." He added that there is a target range and the Central Bank will continue to work for the convergence of inflation and expectations within that range." The president of the BCU also reviewed the main strengths of the country in the current context. He described the main indicators of the financial system as "healthy"; highlighted the credit rating of our country; the low level of the sovereign risk premium and the structure of public debt, both for the residual maturity and for the share of local currency debt in the total public debt. At the same time, he described as "intangible assets" political and social stability, institutional strengths and respect for the rules of the game. The combination of these strengths and assets "means that Uruguay has a very low country risk premium given the global and regional context in which we are immersed", Held. Finally, Graf1a referred to the contribution of the BCU in education, highlighting the more than 40 Interactive Fairs of Economy and Finance held from 2012 to date, and of which more than 70,000 students have already participated. In addition, he highlighted the almost 1000 teachers who were trained by the Bank based on the Teaching Guide on Economics and Finance published together with CAF-Development Bank of Latin America.

Title: Transparency as a new key to international integration
text: May 19 Transparency as a new key to international insertion In the cycle of "Useful Breakfasts" organized by the magazine Somos Uruguay, the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara, made this Wednesday, May 19 at the Sheraton Hotel in Montevideo, a presentation called "The Panama Papers and the long road to transparency" At the beginning of the presentation, Bergara reviewed the fundamental aspects of the international financial crisis, from which a new demand for transparency and higher standards of control is generated. The president of the BCU said in this regard, that "Uruguay has gone from a Focus of opacity towards one of transparency" and that the country must insert itself in the world "based on reputation", which is achieved "through concrete actions of cooperation". Bergara referred to the "significant progress in regulations, institutions and specific results" in the area of money laundering . With numbers that prove it, something similar to what happens in relation to the recommendations for combating the financing of terrorism. He pointed out that "between 2006 and 2009 much progress was made in the FATF recommendations ", with our country having a "better evaluation than 17 of 19 G20 countries". He listed the list of cooperation agreements reached with other countries and highlighted the strengthening of financial intelligence. He stressed that the BCU has strengthened the Financial Information and Analysis Unit (UIAF), generating a sustained increase in suspicious transaction reports every year. However, "the vast majority of reports have been made by banks, and that awareness must also be made by other agents, professionals and financial institutions," he added. Bergara also referred to banking secrecy as an advantage of the "Uruguay financial plaza," which belongs to the past. He said that "a process of easing bank secrecy has begun," in which "we are on the way to minimizing" it and "agents must internalize it since it is a cultural change." Finally , he pointed out that "the world recognizes that we are going in the right direction, since at present the Global Transparency Forum gives us a seal similar to the investment grade." Bergara also recognized the need to incorporate the crime of tax evasion as a precedent for money laundering . "It's a step that needs to be taken," he concluded.

Title: Speech at the Blockchain Summit: Let's not see the stability and development of the financial system as conflicting objectives
text: September 4, 2020 The president of the BCU at the Blockchain Summit: "Let's not see the stability and development of the financial system as opposing objectives" The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, called for thinking about the compatibility that must exist between stability and development of the financial system and said that the objective is to connect the traditional financial system with a type of innovation that allows long-term stability. Labat presented virtually at the Blockchain Summit Uruguay that took place this Friday, September 4. At the beginning of his presentation, called "Technology in the financial sector. Current situation and challenges", the president of the BCU recalled that in a context of global pandemic, the current solidity has allowed the Uruguayan financial system "to be part of the solution and not the problem". Labat stressed that there are pending issues in payment system infrastructure, among other areas, where there is still a certain lag, which is why the disruptions of today's world pose challenges to regulators. "Regulators tend to lag behind; therefore the duty is, perhaps not to go ahead, but to be as close as possible," said the president of the Central Bank. In his presentation, he stated that the solid pillars of stability of the financial system are important for the entire economy and society, and pointed out that sometimes it is raised as an objective opposed to development. "While we have to be careful with stability, which is our priority, we must not see them as opposing objectives. Of course there may be somecatrade-off, but there is a lot to advance in both directions," he said. In this understanding, the president of the Central Bank assured that innovation and competition contribute to development and stability in the long term. "Let's not see the stability and development of the financial system as opposing objectives," he stressed. The president of the Central Bank announced that the objective of the Institution is to resolve and advance in the interconnection between the good of the traditional and the good of innovation. "The solution has to be to find the right connections and adapters so that we can keep all the good things of stability with all the good things of innovation, development and promotion of competition," he said. With a conceptual approach, economist Labat urged to work on innovations based on observing functions, rather than looking at financial institutions, since functions are more stable over time. He also specified that not all technology will fulfill the function more efficiently, so it is convenient to look at the value added by each application that appears in the market. "Not all technology will fulfill financial functions more efficiently," he said, adding that "when a new application appears, we have to ask ourselves, is it doing something? Or is it simply a fa8dade that does not add value?" he asked. To move in that direction, the president of the BCU recalled again that the objective of the BCU is to have a "level playing field" and announced that work is already underway to create the conditions for access without difficulties for new actors. "We are working with several actors on a financialcahubcato promote this," he said. At the end of his presentation, Labat posed to those present the challenge of providing better infrastructure, while at the same time having a financial system that looks abroad based on the comparative advantages that Uruguay has. "Start by looking at how to go abroad, because it is what we have to do and what we deserve," the president of the BCU concluded his presentation.

Title: The president of the BCU Diego Labat urged to think about the development of the financial system in the long term
text: BCU President Diego Labat urged people to think about the development of the financial system in the long term The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Diego Labat, urged to think about the medium and long term to have a better and modern financial system, as he said at the opening of a conference with specialists from the financial industry at the World Trade Center in Montevideo. Labat participated on Wednesday, August 26, as a speaker at a conference on trust in the financial system organized by CFA Society Uruguay, a non-profit institution that brings together financial analysts, portfolio managers and other industry professionals. In his speech, the president of the Central Bank said that the current times are propitious for change in all areas of life and, in particular, in the financial markets, valuing what many Uruguayans have built so far. "Not to come with the intention of changing everything, but to value what has been done so far," Labat reflected. The institution he presides, he said, is aware that the financial business is focused on trust and, for that reason, actions will not focus on a perfect design of the financial system, but on helping to level the playing field. In this sense, the president of the BCU anticipated that work is being done on several initiatives related to the capital market, listening to those who are part of the system, with a focus on building the ground for the private sector to develop, have initiatives and innovate. For this reason, he urged that the private and public sectors work together, each in its role. "It is important that it is clear that public institutions have our duties, but also that the private sector thinks about the medium and long term, building the confidence that leads us to have a much better financial system," the president of the BCU concluded his message.

Title: Inflation is a priority objective of economic policy
text: ADM Lunch Mario Bergara: "Inflation is a priority objective of economic policy" In the cycle of working lunches organized by the Association of Marketing Leaders (ADM) exposed this Wednesday, March 9, the President of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara. The dissertation was entitled "No Overreaction, No Paralysis: Staying the Course " ( . The president of the BCU explained that the global economic situation presents an economic slowdown, the strengthening of the dollar and a fall in international prices, all of them "foreseeable phenomena of the economic cycle". In that sense, Bergara pointed out that Uruguay is no stranger to this situation. In turn, the regional environment presents, according to Bergara, " growth prospects that worsen with each revision", such is the case of Brazil and Argentina. He argued that the combination of the main macroeconomic variables is not favorable in both countries. However, Bergara highlighted the construction of "a platform already proven and that continues to be useful to us to navigate these times." Bergara referred to a "currency depreciation" as important as that of previous periods but with other effects. He stressed the solid financial position of the country and the banking system, in addition to the first place that Uruguay occupies at the end of 2015 in the recognized Latinobarometro.org index in terms of citizen satisfaction with the country's economy. With regard to inflation, the president of the BCU once again ratified that "it is a priority objective of economic policy." In this regard, he maintained that "the economic policy of the BCU is being very contractionary, as it cannot be otherwise." President Bergara insisted once again with other economic policies that allow us to stay the course: exchange rate flexibility that "softens volatility", adequacy of income to the process of economic slowdown, Debt management that mitigates financing risks and the maintenance of investment grade as a relevant asset. On this last point, Bergara pointed out the solid credit rating that our country holds and that indicates the strengths of the Uruguayan economy. The president of the BCU took advantage of the occasion and also announced an increase in bank reserve requirements (increase in the percentage of deposits that financial institutions must keep immobilized in the BCU). In the case of placements in pesos, it will go from 23% to 28% and in dollar deposits, from 26% to 28%.

Title: Speech at ACDE: No one has done more than the BCU to prevent exchange rate misalignment
text: 27 February 2018 Mario Bergara at ACDE: "No one has done more than the BCU to avoid exchange rate misalignment" The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara, spoke this morning with the government economic team at the Forum of the Christian Association of Business Leaders (ACDE). In his speech he referred to the roles of central banks in the current context. Along with Bergara, the Minister of Economy and Finance, Danilo Astori; and the director of the Office of Planning and Budget, alvaro Garcia, participated. "We are living in a world of increasing uncertainty and volatility. It is not easy to have distant horizons for the definition of macroeconomic problems, for small and open countries like Uruguay, "said at the beginning of his presentation ( ) the president of the BCU. decisions." "Since the international financial crisis, developed countries to face liquidity problems, poured huge sums of money into the market. As a consequence, there are four or five times more dollars than 10 years ago and two or three times more euros, therefore there is a lot of capital that needs certain returns and that moves almost in herd behavior. " That is, "everyone takes more or less the same information, and then takes all more or less the same information. For Bergara, a central factor that guides these behaviors is the expectation about the strengthening or weakness of strong currencies, particularly the dollar. "In addition to the fact that we are in a context of uncertainty in relation to the economic policy of developed countries and in particular in the US, it generates volatility in the expectations that agents have about how the dollar is going to move globally." "When there is noise  and the origin of the noise is in US monetary policy  everyone takes refuge in the dollar." Bergara understands that "international financial conditions are conditioning capital flows, and in small countries like ours, they are conditioning pressures on movements in the exchange rate." At the same time, financial markets "do nothing but exacerbate volatility", despite the recent corrections they experienced. For all the above, for Bergara macroeconomic stability is fundamental for the fulfillment of central bank responsibilities. With regard to price stability, the president of the BCU stressed that inflation is within the target range and that "fortunately the process of reducing inflation also brought with it a reduction in expectations about it." Referring to monetary policy, he argued that in addition to being flexible, it is also prudent, responsible and contractionary. On the banking system, he stressed that "the vulnerabilities of other times have been mitigated and that all indicators of the banking system transmit serenity" (solvency, liquidity, delinquency). When referring to the payment system, he emphasized that the promotion of the financial inclusion law, "payments by electronic means have reached a third of the total." On the evolution of the dollar in the current situation, Bergara explained that the dollar in Uruguay accompanies the movements of the dollar in the world. "We have learned that exchange rate flexibility is essential and has served as a 'cushion' to face external shocks." For Bergara there are pressures to exchange rate misalignment due to capital flows, investor portfolio decisions and export earnings (including tourism). "We are concerned about competitiveness, but without drama, since net exports continue to grow and the trade balance continues to show a surplus," he said. He reiterated the need to "follow the trend of the dollar globally ," but also explained that in a small and open country like Uruguay, circumstantial events happen that could generate noises that do not correspond to the fundamentals, and that is when the BCU "intervenes to reduce and soften volatility, preventing excessive appreciations and depreciations." Bergara emphasized the 4 billion dollars purchased by the BCU in the last year, "which undoubtedly has a cost, but that would be much higher if we did it." "It would be a cost to production, employment and social conditions," he added. "No one has done more than the BCU to avoid exchange rate misalignment in our country," he concluded. Title: We have a platform that has already shown strength in challenging situations
text: SPoourtcat i on of the da%(/2PF a Cgionmasu/nDiceafacuillt.n aessp%x)2FPSaglaindaes%Pr2eFnMsa a(r/ioC%om20 bniecragcair an %es2/0Peang% in2a0sC/D%efCa 3ul %t.aAs1pmx)araM%a 2ri0oEBsepr%ga2r0 a2:0"T1e7n%e2mEo asupnx a) plataforma que ya ha mostrado fortalezas ante situaciones desafiantes" (/Comunicaciones/Paginas/Mario%20Bergara%20en%20C%c3%a1mara%20Esp%202017.aspx) May 17, 2017 Mario Bergara: "We have a platform that has already shown strengths in challenging situations" In the cycle Consultation Breakfasts organized by the Official Spanish Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Navigation, the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara, presented this Wednesday, May 17 . The dissertation was titled "Uncertainty is here to stay." The presentation of the president of the BCU was preceded by the welcome made by his counterpart of the Spanish Chamber, Fernando Vidal; and by the Economic and Commercial Counselor of Spain, Antonio Se1nchez Bustamante. Among those present, the presence of the recently appointed ambassador of Spain in Uruguay, Javier Sangro De Liniers, was highlighted. Throughout his dissertation, Bergara explained that "volatility in the world decreased a little, but uncertainty intensified" and that "a world plagued by uncertainties generates risks and opportunities". At the same time, he argued that political processes condition economic and financial processes much more immediately. "Political processes are a necessary ingredient for macroeconomic analysis," he said. For Bergara every political event that is recorded generates a "scrapie", he warned in relation to milestones such as Brexit, the elections in the US and the recent elections in France. "With a statement from a president, the flow of global capital is modified," he said. However, the president of the BCU indicated that "we have a platform that has already shown strengths in challenging situations." "We must have a stable platform that allows us to maintain the course and strategies that remove rigidity and that in turn have the capacity to adapt," he emphasized. Given the uncertainty raised, Bergara calls for an economic policy approach that evaluates risks and with management capacity at different times. He stressed that in this context the importance of price stability in Uruguay is not discussed and that monetary policy has been contractionary to contribute to it. He also highlighted once again the exchange rate flexibility that "smooths out volatility" and the solid financial position of the banking system and the country. Title: The history of the BCU is the history of learning
text: Mario Bergara: "The history of the BCU is the history of learning" The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara, led yesterday the Meeting Line cycle organized by Somos Uruguay at the Sheraton Montevideo Hotel. In the instance called "50 years building the Central Bank of Uruguay", Bergara was accompanied by the first president of the BCU, Enrique V. Iglesias; and the also former president, Ricardo Pascale. Iglesias recalled the context that precipitated the birth of the BCU, based on a plan presented within the framework of the Alliance for Development that included a chapter dedicated to its creation. For Iglesias, "there has always been respect from all governments for the policies of the BCU." In this regard, he stressed that "our country can account for great consensus to respond to problems." In turn, Ricardo Pascale, president of the BCU between 1985 and 1990, reviewed the state of affairs at the end of the dictatorship. "Public trust was completely destroyed" and at the same time "there was great hope in the people," he said. text: SPoou rtca t eda%(/2PF a Cgionmasu/nDiceafacuioltn. aes sp%x)2FPSaglaindas%Pr2eFnMsaar(i/oC%om 20uBniecragcaior an%es2/P0%agEin2a%s8/D0e%fa9uC lt L.aas%px2)0inMst a ituricoioBnearlgid aa r d:%"L2a0eins%tit2u0ceiol%na2li0dsan a dset% sCel3s%oAst9enn%d2e0l dedesl %a r2ro0ld loe"sarrollo%E2%80%9D%2Easpx) (/Comunicaciones/Paginas/Mario%20Bergara%20%e2%80%9cLa%20institucionalidad%20es%20el%20sost%c3%a9n%20del%20desarrollo%e2%80%9d.aspx) April 28 Mario Bergara: "Institutions are the mainstay of development" The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara, spoke on Thursday, April 28, at the conference called "Clear accounts, governance for growth with equity in Latin America and the Caribbean", organized by the World Bank and held at the Punta Cala complex in Montevideo. The conference, which will take place until Friday, brings together leaders from government, the education sector and civil society to discuss the challenges of improving transparency and accountability in public administration in Latin America and the Caribbean. The colloquium revolves around how governance structures affect growth and equity and their linkage to achieve the goals of shared prosperity and poverty reduction in our continent. The president of the BCU participated in the debate on the results of the World Bank's upcoming 2017 World Development Report on governance and the law. The report was presented by Luis Felipe Lopez Calva, co-director of the report, and the debate was also attended by the columnist of the magazine 'The Economist', Michael Reid. Bergara stressed that "institutionality is the support of development" and affirmed that "transparency begins with the government being clear in what it does, its policies and involving society in the design of policies through all its manifestations." He mentioned several examples where mechanisms had been applied to ensure greater transparency in information, including the budget process, the tax system, investment promotion and customs reform. "There are several reforms that include transparency components," he said. Bergara pointed out that from this set of reforms there has been a "leap in quality" by moving "from opacity and discretion to clear rules and transparency." Title: Speech on the exchange rate: You cannot go against global fundamentals
text: March 14, 2018 In the cycle of Working Lunches organized by the Association of Marketing Leaders (ADM) presented this Wednesday, March 14, the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara. The dissertation was entitled "Stability and Growth Despite Global Turbulence" ( ). The president of the BCU began by explaining the current situation and indicating that "every day we receive news that exacerbates uncertainty." "More and more economic and political decisions are influenced not only by what's going on, but by what we all hope is going to happen," he said. For Bergara the signals are confusing, therefore it is difficult to have clear expectations, "having confusing signals about the main variables at the global level is not good news." In the cycle of Working Lunches organized by the Association of Marketing Leaders (ADM) presented this Wednesday, March 14, the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara. The dissertation was entitled "Stability and Growth Despite Global Turbulence" ( ). The president of the BCU began by explaining the current situation and indicating that "every day we receive news that exacerbates uncertainty." "More and more economic and political decisions are influenced not only by what's going on, but by what we all hope is going to happen," he said. For Bergara the signals are confusing, therefore it is difficult to have clear expectations, "having confusing signals about the main variables at the global level is not good news." In this context, Bergara pointed out that the Uruguayan economy evolves healthily from economic growth at decent rates, the recovery of domestic demand, the evolution of exports of goods and services, and a consistent balance of payments current account surplus. However, he also referred to well-defined challenges such as "an orderly fiscal framework but guided by the need for adaptation, a growth that has not yet led to improvements in employment levels and the need to reactivate the investment process". In another passage of his presentation, Bergara provided an overview of the criteria used by the Central Bank to fulfill its responsibilities. With regard to price stability, the president of the BCU stressed that inflation is just above the ceiling of the target range and that "fortunately the process The reduction in inflation also brought with it a reduction in inflation expectations." The president of the BCU affirmed the need to "continue working to consolidate inflation within the target range." In another order, he ratified the "flexible and reasonably contractionary" monetary policy carried out by the BCU. On the banking system, he stressed that "all the indicators of the system transmit serenity." In relation to the payment system, he stressed its modernization to a large extent in the promotion of the Financial Inclusion Law, highlighting that 33% of total payments are made by electronic media". The last passage of his presentation was focused on the evolution of the dollar. In this regard, Bergara reiterated that "you can not go against global fundamentals and that therefore the value of the dollar in Uruguay, accompanies the value of the dollar in the world." For Bergara, "the interventions of the BCU have had an effect of stability, absorbing the excesses (caused by global volatility) in one direction or another." "Because we are responsible, we intervene even at a cost, so that the exchange rate does not collapse and does not have crucial effects on the real sector of the economy," he said. He reiterated that "no one in Uruguay has done more than the Central Bank to keep the dollar essentially competitive and to have bought in the last year four billion dollars. dollars seems to be a sufficient sample."

En otro orden, ratific la poltica monetaria flexible y razonablemente contractiva llevada a cabo por el BCU. Reiter que nadie ha hecho en el Uruguay ms que el Banco Central por mantener el dlar esencialmente competitivo y que haber comprado en el ltimo ao cuatro mil millones de dlares parece ser una muestra suficiente".
