Title: Towards a quality currency
text: d2Hacia una moneda de calidadd3 ??El webinar denominado d2Hacia una moneda de calidadd3 fue organizado por la Facultad de Ciencias Empresariales de la Universidad Cat97lica del Uruguay (UCU) y el Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU).ca The presentation took place on the morning of April 27 and was in charge of the president of the BCU, Diego Labat; and the manager of the Bank's Economic Advisory, Gerardo Licandro. The activity had a few words of welcome from the dean of the Faculty of Business Sciences of the UCU, Isabelle Chaquiriand; and was moderated by the director of the Bachelor's Degree in Economics at the UCU, Emiliano Tealde. In his speech, Labat began by making some reflections such as the need to "look a little beyond" the present and always take into account the temporality of those who are at the head of the institutions, since for the president of the BCU "the construction of public policies must be an accumulation of actions" that in no way acquire a refoundational character. Labat then focused on the aspects that make a quality currency necessary, and highlights that high inflation and dollarization affect long-term growth, harm monetary policy and financial stability. He referred to the non-linear effects of inflation on growth linked to the indexation of the financial system, the fact that dollarization competes with the market in national currency, and the evidence that dollarization affects the financial and real management of Uruguayan companies. Labat said that "monetary policy can anchor expectations in Uruguay." But, he added that "expectations have not been within the range, which is a sign of lack of credibility" and that this is, in large part, the focus of the conflict of objectives. "Monetary policy in recent years anchored inflation expectations, but anchored them between 3-4% above the center of the target range." "We pointed out in the work some problems with the policy instrument," he said. "The reason for not having reached the target range (in the past) was not in the instrument (of using monetary aggregates), but we do believe that the instrument did not help and that the interest rate notoriously has greater virtues than monetary aggregates." ca Labat explained that "the volatility of the interest rate is much greater under aggregate management" and that affects the signals received by market agents. The final block of the presentation was focused on detailing the work agenda of the new monetary policy framework and the de-dollarization and reconstruction of the markets in pesos. Regarding monetary policy, Labat highlighted the main actions carried out in the current period: instrument change; reduction of the inflation target range for September 2022 (3%-6%); driving the overnight bank interest rate and creating a reference range for it; and the concentration of open market operations in shorter periods. He pointed out that "as long as there are no institutional changes, there is much that can be done for the institutional framework in practice," highlighting a "new interpretation of the conflict of objectives," whereby in normal times the inflation target is a priority. In turn, he gave an account of some of the actions for which the BCU has already begun: increasing the frequency of meetings of the Monetary Policy Committee (COPOM); reduction in the frequency of meetings of the Macroeconomic Coordination Committee; as well as improvements in transparency, communication and accountability. In relation to the de-dollarization and reconstruction of the markets in pesos, the president of the BCU highlighted the process of dialogue initiated with the interested parties to achieve in the medium term a de-dollarization of the Uruguayan economy and the consolidation of a quality currency.

La actividad tuvo unas palabras de bienvenida de la decana de la Facultad de Ciencias Empresariales de la UCU, Isabelle Chaquiriand; y cont con la participacin en carcter de moderador del director de la Licenciatura de Economa de la UCU, Emiliano Tealde. En su alocucin, Labat comenz haciendo algunas reflexiones tales como la necesidad de mirar un poco ms all del presente y tener en cuenta siempre la temporalidad de quienes estn al frente de las instituciones, ya que para el presidente del BCU la construccin de las polticas pblicas deben ser una acumulacin de actuaciones que de ninguna manera adquieran un carcter refundacional. A continuacin, Labat se centr en los aspectos que hacen necesaria una moneda de calidad, y destaca que una inflacin alta y la dolarizacin afectan el crecimiento de largo plazo, perjudican la poltica monetaria y la estabilidad financiera. Se refiri a los efectos no lineales de la inflacin sobre el crecimiento vinculados a la indexacin del sistema financiero, a que la dolarizacin compite con el mercado en moneda nacional y a la evidencia que muestra que en Uruguay la dolarizacin afecta la gestin financiera y real de las empresas uruguayas. Labat afirm que la poltica monetaria puede anclar las expectativas en Uruguay. Pero, agreg que las expectativas no han estado dentro del rango, lo que es una muestra de falta de credibilidad y que eso forma, en buena parte, el foco del conflicto de objetivos. La poltica monetaria en los ltimos aos ancl las expectativas de inflacin, pero las ancl entre un 3-4% por encima del centro del rango meta. Sealamos en el trabajo algunos problemas del instrumento de poltica, dijo. La razn de no haber alcanzado el rango meta (en el pasado) no estaba en el instrumento (de uso de agregados monetarios), pero s creemos que el instrumento no ayudaba y que notoriamente tiene mayores virtudes la tasa de inters que los agregados monetarios. Labat explic que la volatilidad de la tasa de inters es mucho mayor bajo manejo de agregados y eso afecta a las seales que reciben los agentes del mercado. El bloque final de la presentacin estuvo enfocado en detallar la agenda de trabajo del nuevo marco de poltica monetaria y la desdolarizacin y reconstruccin de los mercados en pesos. En lo que refiere a la poltica monetaria, Labat destac las principales acciones realizadas en el actual perodo: cambio de instrumento; reduccin del rango objetivo de inflacin para setiembre de 2022 (3% 6 %); conduccin de la tasa de inters bancaria a un da y creacin de un rango de referencia para la misma; y la concentracin de operaciones de mercado abierto en plazos ms cortos. Seal que en tanto no se produzcan cambios institucionales, hay mucho que se puede hacer por la institucionalidad en la prctica, destacando una nueva interpretacin del conflicto de objetivos, por la cual en tiempos normales el objetivo de inflacin es prioritario. A su vez, dio cuenta de algunas de las acciones por las que ya ha comenzado el BCU: aumento de frecuencia de las reuniones del Comit de Poltica Monetaria (COPOM); reduccin de la frecuencia de las reuniones del Comit de Coordinacin Macroeconmica; adems de mejoras en transparencia, comunicacin y rendicin de cuentas. Con relacin a la desdolarizacin y la reconstruccin de los mercados en pesos, el presidente del BCU destac el proceso de dilogo iniciado con las partes interesadas para lograr en el mediano plazo una desdolarizacin de la economa uruguaya y la consolidacin de una moneda de calidad. Title: Speech about the current economic situation and its impact on small and medium-sized companies
text: August 16 President of the BCU spoke about the current economic situation and its impact on small and medium-sized enterprises Invited by the College of Accountants, Economists and Administrators of Uruguay (CCEAU), the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay, Mario Bergara, presented with the aim of bringing the vision of the BCU on the current economic situation of the country and the region. The conference took place yesterday in the event room of the CCEAU and allowed to continue bringing the vision of the BCU to the different actors of society through the promotion of communication and direct participation. The conference entitled "The Uruguayan economy in a challenging context" sought to emphasize those aspects of greatest impact on small and medium-sized enterprises. The president of the CCEAU, Selio Zak, welcomed the realization of this type of instances and advocated an improvement in the competitiveness of SMEs in the current context. Title: The transparency requirements are consistent with our vision and values
text: V Conference on Central Bank Law President of the BCU: "The demands in transparency are consistent with our vision and values" The V Conference on Central Bank Law had today as a corollary the conference "New competences of Central Banking in today's world ( - 01%20V%20Jornadas%20de%20Derecho%20Bancocentralista_Mario%20Bergara.pdf)", by the president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara. After three days of conferences by national and international exhibitors in the Enrique V. Iglesias Room of the BCU, Bergara made a presentation that at the beginning raised a review of the fundamental aspects of the international financial crisis, from which a new demand for transparency and higher standards of control is generated. The president of the BCU said in this regard, that "Uruguay has gone from an approach of opacity to one of transparency" and that today the country "is inserted in the world with seals of transparency and quality that generate reputation." Bergara referred to the "significant progress in regulations, institutions and specific results" in the area of money laundering. He pointed out that "between 2006 and 2009 there was substantial regulatory progress on money laundering and much progress was made in complying with the FATF recommendations," with our country having a better assessment than many of the G20 countries. He listed the list of cooperation agreements reached with other countries and stressed that "today there is a logic of global coordination on transparency." He stressed that the BCU has strengthened the Financial Information and Analysis Unit (UIAF), generating a sustained increase in suspicious transaction reports every year. Bergara also referred to banking secrecy as an advantage of the "Uruguay financial plaza," which belongs to the past. He said that "a process of easing banking secrecy has begun," in which "we are on the way to minimizing" it. "There is a cultural change in relation to banking secrecy and that must be internalized by all agents of society," he said. Finally, he pointed out that "the world recognizes that we are going in the right direction, since at present the Global Transparency Forum gives us a seal similar to the investment grade."

Subray que el BCU ha fortalecido a la Unidad de Informacin y Anlisis Financiero (UIAF), generndose cada ao un aumento sostenido de los reportes de operaciones sospechosas. Bergara tambin se refiri al secreto bancario como una ventaja del Uruguay plaza financiera, que pertenece al pasado. Sostuvo que se ha iniciado un proceso de flexibilizacin del secreto bancario, en el que vamos camino a la minimizacin del mismo. Existe una cambio cultural en relacin al secreto bancario y eso deben internalizarlo todos los agentes de la sociedad, afirm. Title: The preferences of the countries also condition policy decisions
text: August 12, 2016 President of the BCU: "The preferences of the countries also condition the policy decisions" The president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Mario Bergara, reflected on the link between economic policy and the political system during the closing of a meeting co-organized with the Research Institute for Development, Growth and Economics (RIDGE) and the Becker Friedman Institute. In his closing speech of the seminar "The economic and fiscal history of Latin America, Uruguay chapter (1960-2014)", Bergara emphasized that there are several lines of thought at the level of academia that have made it clear that economics as a discipline incorporates political processes , legal and institutional. "We can no longer reason that economists have it clear, we stand on a pedestal, and the problem comes from the political; that vision has been passed over by the academy itself," said the president of the BCU. For that reason, he urged to think that the relationship between economic policies and the political process is not of environment, but of core. In that sense, Bergara mentioned that the preferences of the countries also condition the policy decisions; and as an example he related the case of Uruguay where equity and well-being are a priority for society when making decisions on issues such as the fiscal deficit. In his closing speech , President Mario Bergara stressed that the meeting ratified the capacity for dialogue that exists in Uruguay. "It is a basis to show that we can sit down to dialogue with honesty and criteria even if we have different visions in some things and more consensual in others; that makes us credible," concluded the president of the BCU.

Title: In a changing context, these instances contribute to rethinking economic policy
text: Opening the RIDGE Bergara: "In a changing context, these instances contribute to rethinking economic policy" Economists, international academics and policy makers opened in Montevideo the second meeting of the Research Institute for Development, Growth and Economics (RIDGE), which will have open debate instances at the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU). Welcoming on Tuesday morning, the president of the BCU, Mario Bergara, was grateful and proud to have spaces for debate and exchange of this type, because they allow rethinking economic policy in a changing context and volatility in international markets. "In this new context, with enormous and certain volatility, any academic contribution in order to think and rethink economic policy allows us to face issues and challenges with fresh ideas," he said. In this sense, Bergara was enthusiastic about continuing the work with the International Economic Association (IEA) and the RIDGE. At the Montevideo meeting , academics, professors and policy makers will discuss issues relevant to emerging markets and economies as an exchange of experience and contribution for those designing economic policy at a time of new challenges. As an example of these challenges, Bergara reviewed the current decrease in the price of commodities, the recovery process of the US economy, the growth at lower rates of the Chinese economy and the reverse flow of capital in emerging economies. The RIDGE Forum in Montevideo will have this Tuesday the first open day that is called "Sovereign Debt Sustainability" and will take place from 6:00 p.m. with the participation of the Nobel Prize, Joseph Stiglitz (Columbia University); Jose de Gregorio, (University of Chile); and Jonathan Ostry (IMF).

Title: exchange flexibility is a prerequisite for stability
text: December 18 The president of the BCU affirmed that "exchange rate flexibility is a prerequisite for stability" With the debate on perspectives and challenges for financial stability culminated this Friday the forum organized by the Research Institute for Development, Growth and Economics (RIDGE), which throughout the week took place at the Central Bank of the Uruguay (BCU). The event called "Financial stability outlook and challenges" was attended by the president of the BCU, Mario Bergara; the chief economist for the World Bank region, Augusto de la Torre; and the academic of the Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Xavier Freixas. Economist Augusto de la Torre introduced into the debate the question of how Latin America's financial immune system will cope with the context of a slowing economy. According to the specialist, the slowdown of the regional economy as a whole continues. For De La Torre, the "financial immune system " of countries with exchange rate flexibility, such as Uruguay, is better prepared for the current scenario. For his part, the president of the BCU, Mario Bergara, explained that the characteristics of volatility and uncertainty of this interconnected world are decisive for open and small economies. He affirmed the need to meet the goals "even in turbulent waters." Bergara made it clear that the macro policy approach must consider the risks of the decisions that are taken, in order to seek in this way the greatest stability and, in that sense, stressed that "exchange rate flexibility is a prerequisite." In turn, he realized the need to work actively to soften some market impulses related to international volatility, as well as maintain contractionary monetary policy and make capital inflows profitable. Title: A debate on the management of monetary policy in different economic cycles
text: December 7, 2017 A debate on the management of monetary policy in different business cycles With a debate on the management of monetary policy in the face of the challenges posed by business cycles, the second open debate took place within the Forum of the Research Institute for Development, Growth and Economics (RIDGE). The panel called "The Global Financial Cycle and Financial Stability in Small, Open Economies" took place at the Central Bank of Uruguay, organized by RIDGE together with the BCU and the Financial Stability and Development Network (FSD) of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB). During his presentation, the President of the Central Bank (BCU), Mario Bergara, analyzed the impact of global uncertainty on the expectations of global agents. He also reiterated the existence of "exuberance of financial markets" that present "high liquidity rates that seek returns." "We are probably anticipating the storm and probably the markets are going to adjust," the BCU president stressed. In that sense, he recalled that the adjustment of the markets brings great implications for small economies, which is why today it is very important that monetary policy includes the perspective of risk management. In this area, Bergara also emphasized that when capital flows to emerging economies, challenges to stability are generated. "Today we have an inflow of capital and more de-dollarization that implies pressure on the spot market," he said, adding that if there were no central bank intervention , volatility would have been very bad news. "This must be done by balancing other objectives such as low inflation and competitiveness," Bergara emphasized. The panel was also composed of Ricardo Correa (Federal Reserve of the United States); Giovanni Dell'Arciccia (International Monetary Fund); Graciela Kaminsky (George Washington University) and Donato Masciandaro (Universita Bocconi). Title: Debt sustainability is one of the pillars of macroeconomic stability
text: SPoo u rtc a t i on ofthe da%(/2PF a Cgionmasu/nDiceafacuiolt. naessp%x)2FPSa g a glaindas%Pr2eFnRsaID(G/CEo%m 2uDniPcoclicoyn %e2s/DPD ageibnati on s w it h the ef2aEualt.s apsxp)x) Bergara: "La sustentabilidad de la deuda es uno de los pilar es de la estabilidad macroeconomica" (/Comunicaciones/Paginas/RIDGE-Policy-Debates.aspx) RIDGE Policy Debates 2015 Bergara: "Debt sustainability is one of the pillars of macroeconomic stability" Yesterday took place in the Enrique Iglesias Room of the Central Bank of Uruguay the political debate called "Sustainability of sovereign debt", moderated by the President of the BCU, Mario Bergara, and with the outstanding participation of the American Joseph Stiglitz, winner in 2001 of the Nobel Prize in Economics. The debate is part of the RIDGE Policy Debates, an activity that takes place in Montevideo and Buenos Aires between Monday, November 15 and Friday, November 18 and that promotes debate among economists, academics and government officials. The RIDGE (Research Institute for Devolopment Growth and Economics), the entity that organizes the meeting, is an international center of excellence in economics that works with the most prominent economists from around the world. On this occasion, in addition to Joseph Stiglitz, economists Jose de Gregorio of the University of Chile and Jonathan Ostry of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) participated in the debate. The President of the BCU, in his capacity as moderator, stressed that this debate "is nothing more than understanding and analyzing the public accounts." He explained that the sustainability of public accounts is part of "the perspectives and expectations of the stability of the rules of the game." "Debt sustainability is one of the pillars of macroeconomic stability and therefore of the generation of the right scenario for decision-making in the economic and financial field," Bergara stressed. The beginning of the debate was raised by the IMF economist , Jonathan Ostry, who suggested from recent studies of the international organization itself that there are cases in which the payment of the public debt may not be essential. This is indicated by certain researchers who recognize that some countries can live with their debt given that the costs of maintaining it is a better option than the costs of trying to reduce it. Ostry indicated that there are countries that have less room for maneuver and where debt represents a "serious risk " due to the lack of "fiscal space." In these cases, he explained that there is no debt sustainability and that it must be reduced. However, Ostry argued that a large group of countries can live on their debt. These countries have "fiscal space" because their debt-to-GDP ratio is more reasonable and they can more easily finance their debt in the markets. For his part, Josep Stiglitz indicated that "debt management is a political debate" and that "debt is not a problem." Stiglitz was sympathetic to restructuring as an alternative to debt repayment, something he said "could be even better managed if there were a greater international legal framework." In the same vein, the economist of the University of Chile, Jose de Gregorio, argued that "debts are not paid, they are refinanced." El debate forma parte del RIDGE Policy Debates, actividad que se desarrolla en Montevideo y Buenos Aires entre el lunes 15 y el viernes 18 de noviembre y que promueve el debate entre economistas, acadmicos y funcionarios de gobierno. El RIDGE (Research Institute for Devolopment Growth and Economics), entidad que organiza el encuentro, es un centro internacional de excelencia en economa que trabaja con los economistas ms destacados de todo el mundo. En esta oportunidad, adems de Joseph Stiglitz, participaron del debate los economistas Jos de Gregorio de la Universidad de Chile y Jonathan Ostry del Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI). El Presidente del BCU en su calidad de moderador, destac que dicho debate no es otra cosa que entender y analizar las cuentas pblicas. Explic que la sustentabilidad de las cuentas pblicas forma parte de las perspectivas y expectativas de la estabilidad de las reglas de juego. La sustentabilidad de la deuda es uno de los pilares de la estabilidad macroeconmica y por lo tanto de la generacin del escenario correcto para la toma de decisiones en el terreno econmico y financiero, subray Bergara. El inicio del debate estuvo planteado por el economista del FMI, Jonathan Ostry, quien sugiri a partir de recientes estudios del propio organismo internacional que existen casos en los que el pago de la deuda pblica puede no ser lo esencial. As lo indican ciertos investigadores que reconocen que algunos pases pueden vivir con su deuda dado que los costos de mantenerla es una mejor opcin a los costos de intentar reducirla. Ostry indic que existen pases que tienen menos margen de maniobra y donde la deuda representa un "riesgo grave" debido a la falta de "espacio fiscal". En estos casos, explic que no hay sostenibilidad de la deuda y que sta debe reducirse. No obstante, Ostry sostuvo que un gran grupo de pases puede vivir con su deuda. Estos pases tienen espacio fiscal", dado que su relacin deuda-PIB es ms razonable y pueden financiar con mayor facilidad su deuda en los mercados. Por su parte, Josep Stiglitz indic que el manejo de la deuda es un debate poltico y que la deuda no es un problema. Stiglitz se mostr afn a la reestructuracin como alternativa al pago de la deuda, algo que segn l podra administrase an mejor si existiera un mayor marco legal internacional. En la misma lnea se expres el economista de la Universidad de Chile, Jos de Gregorio, quien argument en relacin a que las deudas no se pagan, se refinancian. Title: Social security systems must be sustainable
text: April 13 President of the BCU: "Social security systems must be sustainable" The challenges posed to regulation by maintaining the sustainability of pension systems in the region was part of the discussion at the opening of the International Seminar "Challenges for individual savings pension systems in the new global scenario", which took place in Montevideo. The event was organized by the International Association of Pension Fund Supervisory Bodies (AIOS) together with the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU). The objective was to discuss and analyze aspects of interest in the social security field. During the opening, the Superintendent of Financial Services (SSF) of the BCU, Juan Pedro Cantera, welcomed the forum, where issues that are a "concern of all societies that seek to increase the quality of life" were discussed, he said. In his message to the attendees, the president of the BCU, Mario Bergara, reviewed the new challenges for regulation in the face of increased longevity and the legitimate demand of citizens for better living conditions. According to the president of the BCU, the current discussion should focus on the existence of nominated accounts rather than who manages the pension funds. "Individual capitalization accounts from an institutional point of view have properties of greater sustainability compared to more unnamed regimes," he said. When it is named, it is more likely to survive scenarios that condition public accounts, said the president of the Central Bank. During a crisis, all the boxes are appealed to, as would happen in the home, Bergara explained and acknowledged that Uruguay in 2002 overcame this obstacle thanks to the existence of the mixed pension system. "We passed the proof that the pension funds were not used, because it had the name of more than a million Uruguayans," he said. The president of the BCU recalled that the reform of social security was due to the fact that the previous system was not sustainable and stressed that the current two-pillar scheme complicates the operation and that is when the challenges for financial regulation. "For there to be a harmonious perspective of many relevant actors, there must be a greater regulatory burden when risks increase," he said. In that sense, the interrelation between markets in the current global context means that risks are transferred from one market to another, so there are greater challenges for regulators, concluded the president of the BCU.

En ese sentido, la interrelacin entre los mercados en el contexto global actual hace que los riesgos se transfieran de un mercado a otro, por lo cual existen mayores desafos para los reguladores, finaliz el presidente del BCU. Title: The vice-president of the BCU spoke to car dealers about the situation and the prospects of the economy
text: July 26, 2022 The vice president of the BCU spoke to automotive dealers about the situation and prospects of the economy The vice president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Washington Ribeiro, spoke to members and directors of the Association of Automotive Brand Dealers (ASCOMA) about the institution's vision regarding the situation and the outlook for the economy. c 3 CPI c 3 CPI "Uguay "Uguay   Target Rank   Target Rank Inflation (var. i.a.) Inflation (var. i.a.) r- c 3 24-month prom expectations In his presentation, called "Economic situation and perspectives: view from the BCU", economist Ribeiro began by reviewing the agenda initiated in 2021 on the need to move towards a quality currency and the new monetary policy framework. He emphasized that high inflation and dollarization not only affect long-term growth, widen the output cycle and harm monetary policy and financial stability, but also "erode household and worker incomes and discourage investment." In this sense, he maintained that "the fight against inflation is in our legal mandate, but it is also what motivates us to work day by day." He then explained the "dual agenda" that was carried out after the declaration of a health emergency in March 2020, with expansive monetary policy and macro-prudential policies, on the one hand, and with the institutionality of monetary policy, on the other. Economist Washington Ribeiro stressed that although expansive monetary policy is contraindicated to combat inflation, it was necessary at that time to maintain liquidity in the economy given the economic circumstances caused by the pandemic. And he listed, one by one, the macro-prudential policies that were carried out, such as the calculation of new credits for reserve requirements, the release of reserve requirements in national currency, the increase in credit maturity terms, the flexibility of accounting standards for the categorization of restructured loans, among others. In relation to the institutional framework of monetary policy, he mentioned the measures that were carried out to this end: the increase in the frequency of meetings of the Monetary Policy Committee (COPOM) with permanent monitoring of the performance of the economy; the messages on the future stance of monetary policy added to the COPOM communique; the incorporation of the minutes of the COPOM meeting; the relaunch of analyst surveys; the schedule of improvements in the Monetary Policy Report (IPOM); the publication of the survey of entrepreneurs of the National Institute of Statistics (INE) led by the BCU; the delivery of a new monetary policy product in newsletter format aimed at businessmen and the general public with a more familiar language, the change of monetary policy instrument from monetary aggregates to interest rates; the reduction of the inflation target range from between 3% and 7% to between 3% and 6%. Ribeiro explained how the BCU adjusted the monetary policy rate to achieve the inflation target taking into account the macroeconomic context: "The transition to interest rates was implemented with the aim of maintaining the expansive instance of monetary policy in an initial phase of the health emergency." "As firm indicators of economic growth were confirmed, together with inflationary pressures and inflation expectations above the target range, the bias of monetary policy became contractionary; however, the body continued to be expansive prior to the Russian conflict in Ukraine." Finally, Ribeiro reiterated that being complacent is not an option: "We ratify our commitment to the target range. The only inflation that is comfortable for us is the one that is located within it." "We are not motivated by orthodoxy but by the conviction that this is a necessary condition to protect the income of Uruguayans, promote financial stability and tend to more investment and work," said the vice president of the BCU.

En relacin con la institucionalidad de la poltica monetaria mencion las medidas que se realizaron a esos efectos: el aumento de frecuencia de reuniones del Comit de Poltica Monetaria (COPOM) con un monitoreo permanente del desempeo de la economa; los mensajes sobre la orientacin futura de la poltica monetaria aadidos al comunicado del COPOM; la incorporacin de la minuta de reunin del COPOM; el relanzamiento de encuesta a analistas; el cronograma de mejoras en el Informe de Poltica Monetaria (IPOM); la publicacin de la encuesta de empresarios del Instituto Nacional de Estadstica (INE) que lidera el BCU; la entrega de un producto nuevo de poltica monetaria en formato newsletter dirigido a empresarios y pblico en general con un lenguaje ms cercano, el cambio de instrumento de poltica monetaria de agregados monetarios a tasa de inters; la reduccin del rango meta de inflacin que pas de ubicarse entre 3% y 7% a entre 3% y 6%. Ribeiro explic cmo el BCU ajust la tasa de poltica monetaria para lograr el objetivo de inflacin teniendo en cuenta el contexto macroeconmico: El pasaje a tasas de inters se implemento con el objetivo de mantener la instancia expansiva de la poltica monetaria en una fase inicial de la emergencia sanitaria. Conforme se constataron indicadores firmes de crecimiento econmico junto con presiones inflacionarias y expectativas de inflacin superiores al rango objetivo, el sesgo de la poltica monetaria se torn contractivo; no obstante la instancia continu siendo expansiva previo al conflicto ruso en Ucrania. Por ltimo, Ribeiro reiter que ser autocomplaciente no es una opcin: Ratificamos nuestro compromiso con el rango meta. La nica inflacin que nos resulta confortable es la que se ubica dentro de ste. No nos motiva la ortodoxia sino la conviccin de que esta es una condicin necesaria para proteger los ingresos de los uruguayos, promover estabilidad financiera y propender a ms inversin y trabajo, dijo el vicepresidente del BCU.

Title: The vice-president of the BCU highlighted the importance of achieving interoperability so that citizens can access the fast payment system
text: June 27, 2023 The vice-president of the BCU stressed the importance of achieving interoperability so that citizens can access the fast payment system Economist Washington Ribeiro highlighted at a meeting in Buenos Aires the recent milestone reached in the implementation of 24/7 instant transfers in Uruguay The Vice President of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Washington Ribeiro, participated on Tuesday, June 27, in a meeting on fast payments held in Buenos Aires and organized by PwC Argentina. The activity, called "PwC Fast Payments & Open Banking Regional Tour", brought together the main industry regulators in the region to discuss growth opportunities and the development of new business models. On the occasion, Ribeiro participated in the panel "Progress of immediate payments in the region: achievements, lessons learned and next steps", together with the director of the Central Bank of the Republic Argentina, Pablo Carreras Mayer; and the Deputy General Manager of Financial Operations of the Central Bank of Paraguay, Liana Caballero. During his presentation, the BCU vice president presented the evolution of the payment system in Uruguay, mentioned the growth space for digital payments and referred to the basic conditions for electronic payments, aspects foreseen in the Roadmap of the Payment System in the country. "In 2023 we set ourselves a fairly ambitious agenda with the generation of a fast payment system," Ribeiro said. In this regard, Vice President Washington Ribeiro indicated that since June 6, 2023, in compliance with the agreed deadline, instant transfers have been operational 24 hours a day, seven days a week. At this time, he recalled that work is being done for the entry into the system of Electronic Money Issuing Institutions (IEDES), with the aim that everyone has access under equal conditions. "We demand certain conditions, including interoperability, which is fundamental," said the vice president. By December 2023, he said that it is expected that person-to-person transfers can be made, based on an alias, and payment in stores with QR codes. To this end, he added that work is being done to strengthen their human and technological capacities within the Payment System Area of the Central Bank; he mentioned the creation of a specific multidisciplinary team focused on the development of fast payments, the creation of a Payment System Committee and the establishment of an Institutional goal in the strategic plan. "We generate instances of dialogue with the financial system," he added; and stressed that actors such as fintechs "are not satellites, but are part of the system." Ribeiro also emphasised the promotion of innovation: "Central Banks tend to be conservative and we understand that it is a value to be so. But without realizing it, we are also innovators, because we are exposed to changes in the situation and we have to adapt our regulations, policies and structures." On this point, he highlighted the NOVA BCU innovation program, which aims to develop research and analysis tasks with the aim of contributing to an adequate regulatory framework for financial innovation. In this line, Ribeiro reported that work has been done on a legal framework for activities with virtual assets, banking and open finance; and the draft Law on the Classification of Cybercrime with the aim of contributing to technological advances generating trust. In the same way, Ribeiro highlighted the recent milestone of the presentation of the Financial Innovation Roundtables where, together with the industry, inputs and proposals will be prepared that can contribute to the study of the impact of innovation on the financial system.

Title: A panel moderated by the vice-president of the BCU, Washington Ribeiro, closed the Annual Economics Conference
text: August 24, 2023 A panel moderated by the vice president of the BCU, Washington Ribeiro, closed the Annual Economics Conference The culmination of the meeting was with an exchange on the current economic context and future prospects to maximize synergies between academia and the real sector The XXXVIII Annual Economics Conference of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU) ended on Wednesday, August 23. The program of the meeting included two international conferences by the doctor in Economics Ana Fostel and the economist Igor Livshits, which addressed issues of financial innovation and the credit market. The president of the BCU, Diego Labat, was in charge of opening the Conference. On the occasion, he stressed that it is on the agenda to advance in innovation and a more developed financial system and emphasized the achievements in terms of inflation. Ana Fostel, professor of economics at the University of Virginia, spoke Tuesday morning about asset prices and financial innovation. Meanwhile, economist Igor Livshits, advisor at the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, gave his dissertation on Wednesday 23 on regulation and information in consumer credit markets. Prior to the presentation of Livshits, Jorge Ponce, manager of Economic Research at the Central Bank, presented a paper on the indebtedness of individuals in Uruguay, co-authored with Rodrigo Arnabal, Santiago Taroco, Cecilia Dassatti and Victoria Landaberry. This research provides information on indebtedness based on information obtained through different sources (Central Credit Risks of the BCU, the company Equifax and others such as the Social Security Bank). The document describes the current situation of the indebtedness of individuals in Uruguay, measures its importance at the local and international level and describes the main characteristics of debtors, focusing on those who are in arrears in the payment of their debts. On Wednesday 23 in the afternoon, the closing of the Annual Economics Conference was with the panel called "Strengthening synergies between academia and the real sector", moderated by the vice president of the BCU, Washington Ribeiro; and with the participation of the rector of the University of the Republic, Rodrigo Arim; the vice-rector of the ORT University, Julio Fernandez; the president of the National Development Agency, Carmen Sanchez and the secretary general of the Uruguayan Chamber of Information Technologies, Amilcar Perea. In the panel, the current economic context and future prospects were exchanged to maximize synergies between academia and the real sector, with the aim of promoting knowledge transfer and effective collaboration between both sectors. During the conversation, Vice President Ribeiro said that for the BCU it is key to integrate these issues into the Conference due to the importance for the country of sustained long-term growth through the efficient use of all the factors of production of the economy, an idea that is expressed through the concept of potential product. "Growing the potential product for Uruguay is a necessity because it will allow us to enrich ourselves, it will allow us to better distribute wealth, it will allow us to prosper and, ultimately, it will allow us to improve the quality of life of our citizens," Ribeiro said.

Title: The vice-president of the BCU said that fintechs "have a place in the financial system"
text: September 19, 2023 The vice president of the BCU said that fintechs "have a place in the financial system" Economist Washington Ribeiro spoke at the Fintech South HUB that brought together entrepreneurs and investors in Montevideo. The vice president of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Washington Ribeiro, said that the fintech sector "has a place in the financial system," since it adds value. Ribeiro made these reflections on September 14, 2023 during his speech at the Fintech South HUB, organized by the Uruguayan Chamber of Fintech and the da Vinci Foundation, which brought together entrepreneurs and investors at the Antel Arena stadium in Montevideo. Among the topics discussed were innovation, companies, entrepreneurship, finance, business and applied technology. The BCU vice president participated in the panel "Beyond 2023: the challenges of regulation in the region", where he stressed that fintechs benefit the traditional financial system by promoting innovation and competition. "What I see is a system that contributes to innovation, in terms of competition, in terms of access, with different services for sectors of the population that traditional banking does not reach. And, above all, it contributes to a more inclusive financial system, with better services and cheaper," Ribeiro said. In this sense, he said that "the business of finance is based on trust," where the Central Bank plays a role in regulating "in due measure," which represents a certificate of protection for users and consumers. Asked about the approach to regulate this sector, Ribeiro explained that the Central Bank tries to understand the business that is being proposed, whether it is a fintech or a traditional institution, identify the risks and, based on that matrix, frame it in the current regulation. "Probably, over the years, the Central Bank  and it is an international trend  will generate much more open regulatory frameworks, in which the entrepreneur can climb the regulation as his business matures and also changes its modalities," he reflected. Asked why the regulatory sandbox is not used in Uruguay , he said that "it would require some legal change" that is not planned in the short term. Regarding how to promote collaboration and fair competition between fintech and traditional banks, the vice president of the Central Bank stressed that the BCU is working to generate different dialogue tables where traditional banking, agents of the financial system and fintechs interact, to generate technological and business interconnection. Ribeiro also mentioned that the Bank is generating, together with the private sector, a boost to the modernization of the payment system in Uruguay: "We believe that fintechs have a role to play there," he said. Economist Ribeiro said that a good part of the advances that occur in the world are thanks to the technology and human capital that Uruguay exports.

Title: The vice-president of the BCU spoke at the VIII Conference on Finance organized by the University of Montevideo
text: November 24, 2023 The vice-president of the BCU spoke at the VIII Finance Conference organized by the University of Montevideo Economist Washington Ribeiro spoke on "Digital Transformation and Payment Methods", where he highlighted the progress in the modernization of the Uruguayan Payment System, in particular, which already exceeded one million instant transfers in September. The Vice President of the Central Bank of Uruguay (BCU), Washington Ribeiro, spoke at the VIII Finance Conference "The Banks of the Future", organized by the Unit of Masters and Postgraduate Degrees in Economics (UMPE) of the University of Montevideo. The Finance Conference took place on Wednesday, November 22 and Thursday, November 23 at the Faculty of Engineering of the University of Montevideo at the LATU (FIUM LATU) and were divided into sessions that included topics on banks in Uruguay and the region; how banks are differentiated today; banks in the context of high interest rates; technological changes: data and artificial intelligence in banks; and digital transformation and payment methods. On this last issue, the economist Ribeiro made his dissertation that began by explaining that the payments project is within the breadth of issues dealt with by the BCU. He spoke about the BCU's strategy in this regard, Nova BCU (the project that articulates the different parts of the BCU in an effort to promote innovation), the Payment System Roadmaps for 2020-2022 and 2023-2025, and the fast payment system. According to Ribeiro, at the international level, it is in payments where the greatest technological changes have been generated and where they are expected to continue to be generated. Regarding the timeline, he highlighted the Compensation Law, which has provided the legal framework for the Uruguayan payment system since 2009; the Financial Inclusion Law of 2014 and the interoperability decree. Ribeiro explained that in 2020 the first Roadmap was generated with certain objectives for the next two years, that in 2022 the modernization of the Payment System through its security, efficiency, accessibility and scalability was updated and that work is currently underway on the 2023-2025 Roadmap: "We understand that the Uruguayan Payment System must be provided with the necessary flexibility so that it can absorb technological changes". He stressed that one of the goals was to complete the multi-acquisition process, which was completed. Also improving compensation systems (the way we transfer money), going to a 24/7 regime, which was also achieved. Then a further step was taken, seeking the instantaneity of transfers, "a key piece to later develop a fast payment system". And, that another goal was to enable the digitization of checks. Ribeiro stressed that all these changes in the financial system with the incorporation of technologies require going hand in hand with cybersecurity. He mentioned that the 2023 - 2025 Payment System Roadmap includes the intention to modify the regulatory frameworks to adapt them to a more modern payment system. During his presentation, Ribeiro said that in the coming months two new milestones promoted by the BCU in its roadmap will be met: the total incorporation of the "alias", which allows transfers between people through the cell phone number, and the implementation of a new modality of payments to businesses through the use of a QR code to make bank transfers. "These two new achievements will contribute to an innovative, accessible, efficient and solid Fast Payment System, which is what we promote at the Central Bank." "Uruguay has a very good level of financial inclusion; it has enormous potential to grow in the usability of that financial system and payment system," Ribeiro said. Regarding the completion in June 2023 of the instant transfer process, he highlighted that in September 2022 there were around 70 thousand instant transfers (which operated within banking hours), while in September 2023 there were more than one million instant transfers. He also highlighted and valued that on average, below 1,000, institutions do not charge for interbank transfers: "We aspire that this threshold will be raised as the transactionality continues to increase." Finally, the vice-president of the BCU pointed out that it is committed to an "interoperable and innovative" payment system, and said that what matters is "to contribute to improving the quality of life of the citizen through our tasks: to lower inflation and with quality and increasingly accessible financial services". To conclude, he mentioned that the intention is to advance in an Open Banking agenda. This will involve, among other things, improving communication channels and the distribution of information among the different participants in the system.
